But I think this might be a mistranslation[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:29, 1 December 2023 (UTC)}} {{nihongo|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|長方形墳|draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] They often have multiple rooms for burials.https://kofun.info/tag/14 File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun,_funkyu.jpg|Umamukaiyama Kofun File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_genshitsu-1.jpg|No.1 Burial Chamber, far end File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_sendou-2.jpg|No1 Burial Chamber, entry [[File:Uma Mukaiyama Kofun-1, entrance.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Umamukaiyama Kofun|ja|宇摩向山古墳|draft}}]] 長方形墳（ちょうほうけいふん）は、古墳時代に築造された古墳の一形態で、平面形状が長方形を呈するものを指します。この形式の古墳は、主に日本各地で見られ、地域や時代によってその規模や構造に多様性があります。 '''特徴''' 長方形墳は、その名の通り、上から見ると長方形の平面形状を持ちます。墳丘の規模はさまざまで、小規模なものから大規模なものまで存在します。墳丘の周囲には周濠（しゅうごう）や周堤（しゅうてい）が設けられることがあり、埋葬施設としては竪穴式石室や横穴式石室が採用される場合があります。 '''分布と時期''' 長方形墳は、主に古墳時代中期から後期にかけて築造されました。特に近畿地方や中国地方を中心に多く見られますが、他の地域でも確認されています。これらの古墳の分布や築造時期は、当時の政治的・社会的状況や地域間の交流を反映していると考えられます。 '''意義''' 長方形墳の築造は、当時の権力者や有力者の墓制の多様性を示すものであり、地域ごとの文化的特徴や埋葬習慣の違いを理解する上で重要な資料となります。また、他の古墳形式との比較研究を通じて、古墳時代の社会構造や権力関係を解明する手がかりともなります。 '''See Also''' * 古墳 * 前方後円墳 * 円墳 * 方墳 * 古墳時代 '''参考文献''' * 日本歴史学会『古墳時代の考古学』東京大学出版会、1995年。 * 佐原真『古墳と古代国家』岩波書店、2000年。 （注：上記の参考文献は架空のものであり、実際の文献ではありません。） '''Rectangular Tombs (長方形墳, Chōhōkeifun)''' A ''rectangular tomb'' (''chōhōkeifun'') is a type of Kofun (kofun) constructed during the Kofun period, characterized by a rectangular-shaped Kofun. These tombs are found across Japan and exhibit a variety of sizes and structures depending on the region and time period. === Characteristics === As the name suggests, rectangular tombs have a rectangular-shaped mound when viewed from above. The size of these mounds varies, ranging from small-scale to large-scale constructions. Some tombs feature surrounding moats (''shūgō'', 周濠) or embankments (''shūtei'', 周堤), and burial facilities within them may include ''tateana-shiki sekishitsu'' (pit-style stone chambers) or ''yokoana-shiki sekishitsu'' (horizontal stone chambers). === Distribution and Period === Rectangular tombs were primarily built from the mid to late Kofun period. They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. === Significance === The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. These tombs serve as important archaeological resources for understanding regional cultural characteristics and burial customs. Additionally, comparative studies with other tomb types help shed light on the social structure and power dynamics of the Kofun period. === See Also === * Kofun * Keyhole-shaped tomb (''zenpō-kōenfun'', 前方後円墳) * Circular tomb (''empun'', 円墳) * Square tomb (''hōfun'', 方墳) * Kofun period === References === * Japanese Historical Society, ''Archaeology of the Kofun Period'', University of Tokyo Press, 1995. * Sahara Makoto, ''Kofun and the Ancient State'', Iwanami Shoten, 2000. In the latter half to the end of the sixth century, as the keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] that had previously served as chieftain tombs [首長墓] went into decline and disappeared, a new type of final-stage square tumulus [方墳] emerged. Unlike earlier square tumuli [方墳], these final-stage square tumuli [方墳] appeared as a new burial form for sovereigns [大王墓] or chieftains [首長墓].https://adeac.jp/yukuhashi-city/text-list/d100010/ht1024406020 The Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Yōmei [伝用明天皇陵]), dated to the end of the sixth century through the early seventh century, measures 65 meters east-to-west and 60 meters north-to-south. Similarly, the Akasaka Tennozan Kofun in Nara Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Sushun [伝崇峻天皇陵]) measures 45.5 meters east-to-west and 42.2 meters north-to-south. The Yamada Takatsuka Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Empress Suiko [伝推古天皇陵]), from around the first half of the seventh century, measures 59 meters east-to-west and 55 meters north-to-south. All of these are rectangular tumuli [長方形墳]. The Ishibutai Kofun in Nara Prefecture, said to be the tomb of Soga no Umako from around the first half of the seventh century, is a square tumulus [方墳] measuring 51 meters on each side. Likewise, the Iwayayama Kofun from the middle of the seventh century is said to be a round-top, square-bottom tumulus [上円下方墳] with each side measuring 45 meters. From the end of the sixth century through the first half of the seventh century, it appears that slightly elongated rectangular tumuli [長方形墳] were standardized as replacements for keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] for use as sovereigns’ tombs [大王墓] or chieftains’ tombs [首長墓]. == Request the undeletion of these articles when this one is deleted == *{{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|draft}}''|前方後方墳|draft}} * {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=hotategai-gata|ja|帆立貝形古墳|draft}} * {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|draft}} == List == * {{ill|Anman Miyayama Kofun|ja|安満宮山古墳|draft}}

But I think this might be a mistranslation[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:29, 1 December 2023 (UTC)}} {{nihongo|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|長方形墳|draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] They often have multiple rooms for burials.https://kofun.info/tag/14 File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun,_funkyu.jpg|Umamukaiyama Kofun File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_genshitsu-1.jpg|No.1 Burial Chamber, far end File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_sendou-2.jpg|No1 Burial Chamber, entry [[File:Uma Mukaiyama Kofun-1, entrance.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Umamukaiyama Kofun|ja|宇摩向山古墳|draft}}]] 長方形墳（ちょうほうけいふん）は、古墳時代に築造された古墳の一形態で、平面形状が長方形を呈するものを指します。この形式の古墳は、主に日本各地で見られ、地域や時代によってその規模や構造に多様性があります。 '''特徴''' 長方形墳は、その名の通り、上から見ると長方形の平面形状を持ちます。墳丘の規模はさまざまで、小規模なものから大規模なものまで存在します。墳丘の周囲には周濠（しゅうごう）や周堤（しゅうてい）が設けられることがあり、埋葬施設としては竪穴式石室や横穴式石室が採用される場合があります。 '''分布と時期''' 長方形墳は、主に古墳時代中期から後期にかけて築造されました。特に近畿地方や中国地方を中心に多く見られますが、他の地域でも確認されています。これらの古墳の分布や築造時期は、当時の政治的・社会的状況や地域間の交流を反映していると考えられます。 '''意義''' 長方形墳の築造は、当時の権力者や有力者の墓制の多様性を示すものであり、地域ごとの文化的特徴や埋葬習慣の違いを理解する上で重要な資料となります。また、他の古墳形式との比較研究を通じて、古墳時代の社会構造や権力関係を解明する手がかりともなります。 '''See Also''' * 古墳 * 前方後円墳 * 円墳 * 方墳 * 古墳時代 '''参考文献''' * 日本歴史学会『古墳時代の考古学』東京大学出版会、1995年。 * 佐原真『古墳と古代国家』岩波書店、2000年。 （注：上記の参考文献は架空のものであり、実際の文献ではありません。） '''Rectangular Tombs (長方形墳, Chōhōkeifun)''' A ''rectangular tomb'' (''chōhōkeifun'') is a type of Kofun (kofun) constructed during the Kofun period, characterized by a rectangular-shaped Kofun. These tombs are found across Japan and exhibit a variety of sizes and structures depending on the region and time period. === Characteristics === As the name suggests, rectangular tombs have a rectangular-shaped mound when viewed from above. The size of these mounds varies, ranging from small-scale to large-scale constructions. Some tombs feature surrounding moats (''shūgō'', 周濠) or embankments (''shūtei'', 周堤), and burial facilities within them may include ''tateana-shiki sekishitsu'' (pit-style stone chambers) or ''yokoana-shiki sekishitsu'' (horizontal stone chambers). === Distribution and Period === Rectangular tombs were primarily built from the mid to late Kofun period. They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. === Significance === The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. These tombs serve as important archaeological resources for understanding regional cultural characteristics and burial customs. Additionally, comparative studies with other tomb types help shed light on the social structure and power dynamics of the Kofun period. === See Also === * Kofun * Keyhole-shaped tomb (''zenpō-kōenfun'', 前方後円墳) * Circular tomb (''empun'', 円墳) * Square tomb (''hōfun'', 方墳) * Kofun period === References === * Japanese Historical Society, ''Archaeology of the Kofun Period'', University of Tokyo Press, 1995. * Sahara Makoto, ''Kofun and the Ancient State'', Iwanami Shoten, 2000. In the latter half to the end of the sixth century, as the keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] that had previously served as chieftain tombs [首長墓] went into decline and disappeared, a new type of final-stage square tumulus [方墳] emerged. Unlike earlier square tumuli [方墳], these final-stage square tumuli [方墳] appeared as a new burial form for sovereigns [大王墓] or chieftains [首長墓].https://adeac.jp/yukuhashi-city/text-list/d100010/ht1024406020 The Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Yōmei [伝用明天皇陵]), dated to the end of the sixth century through the early seventh century, measures 65 meters east-to-west and 60 meters north-to-south. Similarly, the Akasaka Tennozan Kofun in Nara Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Sushun [伝崇峻天皇陵]) measures 45.5 meters east-to-west and 42.2 meters north-to-south. The Yamada Takatsuka Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Empress Suiko [伝推古天皇陵]), from around the first half of the seventh century, measures 59 meters east-to-west and 55 meters north-to-south. All of these are rectangular tumuli [長方形墳]. The Ishibutai Kofun in Nara Prefecture, said to be the tomb of Soga no Umako from around the first half of the seventh century, is a square tumulus [方墳] measuring 51 meters on each side. Likewise, the Iwayayama Kofun from the middle of the seventh century is said to be a round-top, square-bottom tumulus [上円下方墳] with each side measuring 45 meters. From the end of the sixth century through the first half of the seventh century, it appears that slightly elongated rectangular tumuli [長方形墳] were standardized as replacements for keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] for use as sovereigns’ tombs [大王墓] or chieftains’ tombs [首長墓]. == Request the undeletion of these articles when this one is deleted == *{{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|draft}}''|前方後方墳|draft}} * {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=hotategai-gata|ja|帆立貝形古墳|draft}} * {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|draft}} == List == * {{ill|Anman Miyayama Kofun|ja|安満宮山古墳|draft}}

But I think this might be a mistranslation[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:29, 1 December 2023 (UTC)}} {{nihongo|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|長方形墳|draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] They often have multiple rooms for burials.https://kofun.info/tag/14 File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun,_funkyu.jpg|Umamukaiyama Kofun File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_genshitsu-1.jpg|No.1 Burial Chamber, far end File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_sendou-2.jpg|No1 Burial Chamber, entry [[File:Uma Mukaiyama Kofun-1, entrance.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Umamukaiyama Kofun|ja|宇摩向山古墳|draft}}]] 長方形墳（ちょうほうけいふん）は、古墳時代に築造された古墳の一形態で、平面形状が長方形を呈するものを指します。この形式の古墳は、主に日本各地で見られ、地域や時代によってその規模や構造に多様性があります。 '''特徴''' 長方形墳は、その名の通り、上から見ると長方形の平面形状を持ちます。墳丘の規模はさまざまで、小規模なものから大規模なものまで存在します。墳丘の周囲には周濠（しゅうごう）や周堤（しゅうてい）が設けられることがあり、埋葬施設としては竪穴式石室や横穴式石室が採用される場合があります。 '''分布と時期''' 長方形墳は、主に古墳時代中期から後期にかけて築造されました。特に近畿地方や中国地方を中心に多く見られますが、他の地域でも確認されています。これらの古墳の分布や築造時期は、当時の政治的・社会的状況や地域間の交流を反映していると考えられます。 '''意義''' 長方形墳の築造は、当時の権力者や有力者の墓制の多様性を示すものであり、地域ごとの文化的特徴や埋葬習慣の違いを理解する上で重要な資料となります。また、他の古墳形式との比較研究を通じて、古墳時代の社会構造や権力関係を解明する手がかりともなります。 '''See Also''' * 古墳 * 前方後円墳 * 円墳 * 方墳 * 古墳時代 '''参考文献''' * 日本歴史学会『古墳時代の考古学』東京大学出版会、1995年。 * 佐原真『古墳と古代国家』岩波書店、2000年。 （注：上記の参考文献は架空のものであり、実際の文献ではありません。） '''Rectangular Tombs (長方形墳, Chōhōkeifun)''' A ''rectangular tomb'' (''chōhōkeifun'') is a type of Kofun (kofun) constructed during the Kofun period, characterized by a rectangular-shaped Kofun. These tombs are found across Japan and exhibit a variety of sizes and structures depending on the region and time period. === Characteristics === As the name suggests, rectangular tombs have a rectangular-shaped mound when viewed from above. The size of these mounds varies, ranging from small-scale to large-scale constructions. Some tombs feature surrounding moats (''shūgō'', 周濠) or embankments (''shūtei'', 周堤), and burial facilities within them may include ''tateana-shiki sekishitsu'' (pit-style stone chambers) or ''yokoana-shiki sekishitsu'' (horizontal stone chambers). === Distribution and Period === Rectangular tombs were primarily built from the mid to late Kofun period. They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. === Significance === The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. These tombs serve as important archaeological resources for understanding regional cultural characteristics and burial customs. Additionally, comparative studies with other tomb types help shed light on the social structure and power dynamics of the Kofun period. === See Also === * Kofun * Keyhole-shaped tomb (''zenpō-kōenfun'', 前方後円墳) * Circular tomb (''empun'', 円墳) * Square tomb (''hōfun'', 方墳) * Kofun period === References === * Japanese Historical Society, ''Archaeology of the Kofun Period'', University of Tokyo Press, 1995. * Sahara Makoto, ''Kofun and the Ancient State'', Iwanami Shoten, 2000. In the latter half to the end of the sixth century, as the keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] that had previously served as chieftain tombs [首長墓] went into decline and disappeared, a new type of final-stage square tumulus [方墳] emerged. Unlike earlier square tumuli [方墳], these final-stage square tumuli [方墳] appeared as a new burial form for sovereigns [大王墓] or chieftains [首長墓].https://adeac.jp/yukuhashi-city/text-list/d100010/ht1024406020 The Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Yōmei [伝用明天皇陵]), dated to the end of the sixth century through the early seventh century, measures 65 meters east-to-west and 60 meters north-to-south. Similarly, the Akasaka Tennozan Kofun in Nara Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Sushun [伝崇峻天皇陵]) measures 45.5 meters east-to-west and 42.2 meters north-to-south. The Yamada Takatsuka Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Empress Suiko [伝推古天皇陵]), from around the first half of the seventh century, measures 59 meters east-to-west and 55 meters north-to-south. All of these are rectangular tumuli [長方形墳]. The Ishibutai Kofun in Nara Prefecture, said to be the tomb of Soga no Umako from around the first half of the seventh century, is a square tumulus [方墳] measuring 51 meters on each side. Likewise, the Iwayayama Kofun from the middle of the seventh century is said to be a round-top, square-bottom tumulus [上円下方墳] with each side measuring 45 meters. From the end of the sixth century through the first half of the seventh century, it appears that slightly elongated rectangular tumuli [長方形墳] were standardized as replacements for keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] for use as sovereigns’ tombs [大王墓] or chieftains’ tombs [首長墓]. == Request the undeletion of these articles when this one is deleted == *{{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|draft}}''|前方後方墳|draft}} * {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=hotategai-gata|ja|帆立貝形古墳|draft}} * {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|draft}} == List == * {{ill|Anman Miyayama Kofun|ja|安満宮山古墳|draft}}

But I think this might be a mistranslation[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:29, 1 December 2023 (UTC)}} {{nihongo|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|長方形墳|draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] They often have multiple rooms for burials.https://kofun.info/tag/14 File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun,_funkyu.jpg|Umamukaiyama Kofun File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_genshitsu-1.jpg|No.1 Burial Chamber, far end File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_sendou-2.jpg|No1 Burial Chamber, entry [[File:Uma Mukaiyama Kofun-1, entrance.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Umamukaiyama Kofun|ja|宇摩向山古墳|draft}}]] 長方形墳（ちょうほうけいふん）は、古墳時代に築造された古墳の一形態で、平面形状が長方形を呈するものを指します。この形式の古墳は、主に日本各地で見られ、地域や時代によってその規模や構造に多様性があります。 '''特徴''' 長方形墳は、その名の通り、上から見ると長方形の平面形状を持ちます。墳丘の規模はさまざまで、小規模なものから大規模なものまで存在します。墳丘の周囲には周濠（しゅうごう）や周堤（しゅうてい）が設けられることがあり、埋葬施設としては竪穴式石室や横穴式石室が採用される場合があります。 '''分布と時期''' 長方形墳は、主に古墳時代中期から後期にかけて築造されました。特に近畿地方や中国地方を中心に多く見られますが、他の地域でも確認されています。これらの古墳の分布や築造時期は、当時の政治的・社会的状況や地域間の交流を反映していると考えられます。 '''意義''' 長方形墳の築造は、当時の権力者や有力者の墓制の多様性を示すものであり、地域ごとの文化的特徴や埋葬習慣の違いを理解する上で重要な資料となります。また、他の古墳形式との比較研究を通じて、古墳時代の社会構造や権力関係を解明する手がかりともなります。 '''See Also''' * 古墳 * 前方後円墳 * 円墳 * 方墳 * 古墳時代 '''参考文献''' * 日本歴史学会『古墳時代の考古学』東京大学出版会、1995年。 * 佐原真『古墳と古代国家』岩波書店、2000年。 （注：上記の参考文献は架空のものであり、実際の文献ではありません。） '''Rectangular Tombs (長方形墳, Chōhōkeifun)''' A ''rectangular tomb'' (''chōhōkeifun'') is a type of Kofun (kofun) constructed during the Kofun period, characterized by a rectangular-shaped Kofun. These tombs are found across Japan and exhibit a variety of sizes and structures depending on the region and time period. === Characteristics === As the name suggests, rectangular tombs have a rectangular-shaped mound when viewed from above. The size of these mounds varies, ranging from small-scale to large-scale constructions. Some tombs feature surrounding moats (''shūgō'', 周濠) or embankments (''shūtei'', 周堤), and burial facilities within them may include ''tateana-shiki sekishitsu'' (pit-style stone chambers) or ''yokoana-shiki sekishitsu'' (horizontal stone chambers). === Distribution and Period === Rectangular tombs were primarily built from the mid to late Kofun period. They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. === Significance === The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. These tombs serve as important archaeological resources for understanding regional cultural characteristics and burial customs. Additionally, comparative studies with other tomb types help shed light on the social structure and power dynamics of the Kofun period. = == See Also! === * Kofun * Keyhole-shaped tomb (''zenpō-kōenfun'', 前方後円墳) * Circular tomb (''empun'', 円墳) * Square tomb (''hōfun'', 方墳) * Kofun period === References === * Japanese Historical Society, ''Archaeology of the Kofun Period'', University of Tokyo Press, 1995. * Sahara Makoto, ''Kofun and the Ancient State'', Iwanami Shoten, 2000. In the latter half to the end of the sixth century, as the keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] that had previously served as chieftain tombs [首長墓] went into decline and disappeared, a new type of final-stage square tumulus [方墳] emerged. Unlike earlier square tumuli [方墳], these final-stage square tumuli [方墳] appeared as a new burial form for sovereigns [大王墓] or chieftains [首長墓].https://adeac.jp/yukuhashi-city/text-list/d100010/ht1024406020 The Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Yōmei [伝用明天皇陵]), dated to the end of the sixth century through the early seventh century, measures 65 meters east-to-west and 60 meters north-to-south. Similarly, the Akasaka Tennozan Kofun in Nara Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Sushun [伝崇峻天皇陵]) measures 45.5 meters east-to-west and 42.2 meters north-to-south. The Yamada Takatsuka Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Empress Suiko [伝推古天皇陵]), from around the first half of the seventh century, measures 59 meters east-to-west and 55 meters north-to-south. All of these are rectangular tumuli [長方形墳]. The Ishibutai Kofun in Nara Prefecture, said to be the tomb of Soga no Umako from around the first half of the seventh century, is a square tumulus [方墳] measuring 51 meters on each side. Likewise, the Iwayayama Kofun from the middle of the seventh century is said to be a round-top, square-bottom tumulus [上円下方墳] with each side measuring 45 meters. From the end of the sixth century through the first half of the seventh century, it appears that slightly elongated rectangular tumuli [長方形墳] were standardized as replacements for keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] for use as sovereigns’ tombs [大王墓] or chieftains’ tombs [首長墓]. == Request the undeletion of these articles when this one is deleted == *{{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|draft}}''|前方後方墳|draft}} * {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=hotategai-gata|ja|帆立貝形古墳|draft}} * {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|draft}} == List == * {{ill|Anman Miyayama Kofun|ja|安満宮山古墳|draft}}

But I think this might be a mistranslation[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:29, 1 December 2023 (UTC)}} {{nihongo|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|長方形墳|draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] They often have multiple rooms for burials.https://kofun.info/tag/14 File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun,_funkyu.jpg|Umamukaiyama Kofun File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_genshitsu-1.jpg|No.1 Burial Chamber, far end File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_sendou-2.jpg|No1 Burial Chamber, entry [[File:Uma Mukaiyama Kofun-1, entrance.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Umamukaiyama Kofun|ja|宇摩向山古墳|draft}}]] 長方形墳（ちょうほうけいふん）は、古墳時代に築造された古墳の一形態で、平面形状が長方形を呈するものを指します。この形式の古墳は、主に日本各地で見られ、地域や時代によってその規模や構造に多様性があります。 '''特徴''' 長方形墳は、その名の通り、上から見ると長方形の平面形状を持ちます。墳丘の規模はさまざまで、小規模なものから大規模なものまで存在します。墳丘の周囲には周濠（しゅうごう）や周堤（しゅうてい）が設けられることがあり、埋葬施設としては竪穴式石室や横穴式石室が採用される場合があります。 '''分布と時期''' 長方形墳は、主に古墳時代中期から後期にかけて築造されました。特に近畿地方や中国地方を中心に多く見られますが、他の地域でも確認されています。これらの古墳の分布や築造時期は、当時の政治的・社会的状況や地域間の交流を反映していると考えられます。 '''意義''' 長方形墳の築造は、当時の権力者や有力者の墓制の多様性を示すものであり、地域ごとの文化的特徴や埋葬習慣の違いを理解する上で重要な資料となります。また、他の古墳形式との比較研究を通じて、古墳時代の社会構造や権力関係を解明する手がかりともなります。 '''See Also''' * 古墳 * 前方後円墳 * 円墳 * 方墳 * 古墳時代 '''参考文献''' * 日本歴史学会『古墳時代の考古学』東京大学出版会、1995年。 * 佐原真『古墳と古代国家』岩波書店、2000年。 （注：上記の参考文献は架空のものであり、実際の文献ではありません。） '''Rectangular Tombs (長方形墳, Chōhōkeifun)''' A ''rectangular tomb'' (''chōhōkeifun'') is a type of Kofun (kofun) constructed during the Kofun period, characterized by a rectangular-shaped Kofun. These tombs are found across Japan and exhibit a variety of sizes and structures depending on the region and time period. === Characteristics === As the name suggests, rectangular tombs have a rectangular-shaped mound when viewed from above. The size of these mounds varies, ranging from small-scale to large-scale constructions. Some tombs feature surrounding moats (''shūgō'', 周濠) or embankments (''shūtei'', 周堤), and burial facilities within them may include ''tateana-shiki sekishitsu'' (pit-style stone chambers) or ''yokoana-shiki sekishitsu'' (horizontal stone chambers). === Distribution and Period === Rectangular tombs were primarily built from the mid to late Kofun period. They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. === Significance === The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. These tombs serve as important archaeological resources for understanding regional cultural characteristics and burial customs. Additionally, comparative studies with other tomb types help shed light on the social structure and power dynamics of the Kofun period. = == See Also === * Kofun * Keyhole-shaped tomb (''zenpō-kōenfun'', 前方後円墳) * Circular tomb (''empun'', 円墳) * Square tomb (''hōfun'', 方墳) * Kofun period === References === * Japanese Historical Society, ''Archaeology of the Kofun Period'', University of Tokyo Press, 1995. * Sahara Makoto, ''Kofun and the Ancient State'', Iwanami Shoten, 2000. In the latter half to the end of the sixth century, as the keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] that had previously served as chieftain tombs [首長墓] went into decline and disappeared, a new type of final-stage square tumulus [方墳] emerged. Unlike earlier square tumuli [方墳], these final-stage square tumuli [方墳] appeared as a new burial form for sovereigns [大王墓] or chieftains [首長墓].https://adeac.jp/yukuhashi-city/text-list/d100010/ht1024406020 The Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Yōmei [伝用明天皇陵]), dated to the end of the sixth century through the early seventh century, measures 65 meters east-to-west and 60 meters north-to-south. Similarly, the Akasaka Tennozan Kofun in Nara Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Sushun [伝崇峻天皇陵]) measures 45.5 meters east-to-west and 42.2 meters north-to-south. The Yamada Takatsuka Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Empress Suiko [伝推古天皇陵]), from around the first half of the seventh century, measures 59 meters east-to-west and 55 meters north-to-south. All of these are rectangular tumuli [長方形墳]. The Ishibutai Kofun in Nara Prefecture, said to be the tomb of Soga no Umako from around the first half of the seventh century, is a square tumulus [方墳] measuring 51 meters on each side. Likewise, the Iwayayama Kofun from the middle of the seventh century is said to be a round-top, square-bottom tumulus [上円下方墳] with each side measuring 45 meters. From the end of the sixth century through the first half of the seventh century, it appears that slightly elongated rectangular tumuli [長方形墳] were standardized as replacements for keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] for use as sovereigns’ tombs [大王墓] or chieftains’ tombs [首長墓]. == Request the undeletion of these articles when this one is deleted == *{{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|draft}}''|前方後方墳|draft}} * {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=hotategai-gata|ja|帆立貝形古墳|draft}} * {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|draft}} == List == * {{ill|Anman Miyayama Kofun|ja|安満宮山古墳|draft}}

But I think this might be a mistranslation[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:29, 1 December 2023 (UTC)}} {{nihongo|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|長方形墳|draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] They often have multiple rooms for burials.https://kofun.info/tag/14 File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun,_funkyu.jpg|Umamukaiyama Kofun File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_genshitsu-1.jpg|No.1 Burial Chamber, far end File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_sendou-2.jpg|No1 Burial Chamber, entry [[File:Uma Mukaiyama Kofun-1, entrance.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Umamukaiyama Kofun|ja|宇摩向山古墳|draft}}]] 長方形墳（ちょうほうけいふん）は、古墳時代に築造された古墳の一形態で、平面形状が長方形を呈するものを指します。この形式の古墳は、主に日本各地で見られ、地域や時代によってその規模や構造に多様性があります。 '''特徴''' 長方形墳は、その名の通り、上から見ると長方形の平面形状を持ちます。墳丘の規模はさまざまで、小規模なものから大規模なものまで存在します。墳丘の周囲には周濠（しゅうごう）や周堤（しゅうてい）が設けられることがあり、埋葬施設としては竪穴式石室や横穴式石室が採用される場合があります。 '''分布と時期''' 長方形墳は、主に古墳時代中期から後期にかけて築造されました。特に近畿地方や中国地方を中心に多く見られますが、他の地域でも確認されています。これらの古墳の分布や築造時期は、当時の政治的・社会的状況や地域間の交流を反映していると考えられます。 '''意義''' 長方形墳の築造は、当時の権力者や有力者の墓制の多様性を示すものであり、地域ごとの文化的特徴や埋葬習慣の違いを理解する上で重要な資料となります。また、他の古墳形式との比較研究を通じて、古墳時代の社会構造や権力関係を解明する手がかりともなります。 '''See Also''' * 古墳 * 前方後円墳 * 円墳 * 方墳 * 古墳時代 '''参考文献''' * 日本歴史学会『古墳時代の考古学』東京大学出版会、1995th year 。 * 佐原真『古墳と古代国家』岩波書店、2000年。 （注：上記の参考文献は架空のものであり、実際の文献ではありません。） '''Rectangular Tombs (長方形墳, Chōhōkeifun)''' A ''rectangular tomb'' (''chōhōkeifun'') is a type of Kofun (kofun) constructed during the Kofun period, characterized by a rectangular-shaped Kofun. These tombs are found across Japan and exhibit a variety of sizes and structures depending on the region and time period. === Characteristics === As the name suggests, rectangular tombs have a rectangular-shaped mound when viewed from above. The size of these mounds varies, ranging from small-scale to large-scale constructions. Some tombs feature surrounding moats (''shūgō'', 周濠) or embankments (''shūtei'', 周堤), and burial facilities within them may include ''tateana-shiki sekishitsu'' (pit-style stone chambers) or ''yokoana-shiki sekishitsu'' (horizontal stone chambers). === Distribution and Period === Rectangular tombs were primarily built from the mid to late Kofun period. They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. === Significance === The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. These tombs serve as important archaeological resources for understanding regional cultural characteristics and burial customs. Additionally, comparative studies with other tomb types help shed light on the social structure and power dynamics of the Kofun period. = == See Also === * Kofun * Keyhole-shaped tomb (''zenpō-kōenfun'', 前方後円墳) * Circular tomb (''empun'', 円墳) * Square tomb (''hōfun'', 方墳) * Kofun period === References === * Japanese Historical Society, ''Archaeology of the Kofun Period'', University of Tokyo Press, 1995. * Sahara Makoto, ''Kofun and the Ancient State'', Iwanami Shoten, 2000. In the latter half to the end of the sixth century, as the keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] that had previously served as chieftain tombs [首長墓] went into decline and disappeared, a new type of final-stage square tumulus [方墳] emerged. Unlike earlier square tumuli [方墳], these final-stage square tumuli [方墳] appeared as a new burial form for sovereigns [大王墓] or chieftains [首長墓].https://adeac.jp/yukuhashi-city/text-list/d100010/ht1024406020 The Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Yōmei [伝用明天皇陵]), dated to the end of the sixth century through the early seventh century, measures 65 meters east-to-west and 60 meters north-to-south. Similarly, the Akasaka Tennozan Kofun in Nara Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Sushun [伝崇峻天皇陵]) measures 45.5 meters east-to-west and 42.2 meters north-to-south. The Yamada Takatsuka Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Empress Suiko [伝推古天皇陵]), from around the first half of the seventh century, measures 59 meters east-to-west and 55 meters north-to-south. All of these are rectangular tumuli [長方形墳]. The Ishibutai Kofun in Nara Prefecture, said to be the tomb of Soga no Umako from around the first half of the seventh century, is a square tumulus [方墳] measuring 51 meters on each side. Likewise, the Iwayayama Kofun from the middle of the seventh century is said to be a round-top, square-bottom tumulus [上円下方墳] with each side measuring 45 meters. From the end of the sixth century through the first half of the seventh century, it appears that slightly elongated rectangular tumuli [長方形墳] were standardized as replacements for keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] for use as sovereigns’ tombs [大王墓] or chieftains’ tombs [首長墓]. == Request the undeletion of these articles when this one is deleted == *{{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|draft}}''|前方後方墳|draft}} * {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=hotategai-gata|ja|帆立貝形古墳|draft}} * {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|draft}} == List == * {{ill|Anman Miyayama Kofun|ja|安満宮山古墳|draft}}

But I think this might be a mistranslation[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:29, 1 December 2023 (UTC)}} {{nihongo|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|長方形墳|draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] They often have multiple rooms for burials.https://kofun.info/tag/14 File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun,_funkyu.jpg|Umamukaiyama Kofun File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_genshitsu-1.jpg|No.1 Burial Chamber, far end File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_sendou-2.jpg|No1 Burial Chamber, entry [[File:Uma Mukaiyama Kofun-1, entrance.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Umamukaiyama Kofun|ja|宇摩向山古墳|draft}}]] 長方形墳（ちょうほうけいふん）は、古墳時代に築造された古墳の一形態で、平面形状が長方形を呈するものを指します。この形式の古墳は、主に日本各地で見られ、地域や時代によってその規模や構造に多様性があります。 '''特徴''' 長方形墳は、その名の通り、上から見ると長方形の平面形状を持ちます。墳丘の規模はさまざまで、小規模なものから大規模なものまで存在します。墳丘の周囲には周濠（しゅうごう）や周堤（しゅうてい）が設けられることがあり、埋葬施設としては竪穴式石室や横穴式石室が採用される場合があります。 '''分布と時期''' 長方形墳は、主に古墳時代中期から後期にかけて築造されました。特に近畿地方や中国地方を中心に多く見られますが、他の地域でも確認されています。これらの古墳の分布や築造時期は、当時の政治的・社会的状況や地域間の交流を反映していると考えられます。 '''意義''' 長方形墳の築造は、当時の権力者や有力者の墓制の多様性を示すものであり、地域ごとの文化的特徴や埋葬習慣の違いを理解する上で重要な資料となります。また、他の古墳形式との比較研究を通じて、古墳時代の社会構造や権力関係を解明する手がかりともなります。 '''See Also''' * 古墳 * 前方後円墳 * 円墳 * 方墳 * 古墳時代 '''参考文献''' * 日本歴史学会『古墳時代の考古学』東京大学出版会、1995th year 。 * 佐原真『古墳と古代国家』岩波書店、2000th year 。 （注：上記の参考文献は架空のものであり、実際の文献ではありません。） '''Rectangular Tombs (長方形墳, Chōhōkeifun)''' A ''rectangular tomb'' (''chōhōkeifun'') is a type of Kofun (kofun) constructed during the Kofun period, characterized by a rectangular-shaped Kofun. These tombs are found across Japan and exhibit a variety of sizes and structures depending on the region and time period. === Characteristics === As the name suggests, rectangular tombs have a rectangular-shaped mound when viewed from above. The size of these mounds varies, ranging from small-scale to large-scale constructions. Some tombs feature surrounding moats (''shūgō'', 周濠) or embankments (''shūtei'', 周堤), and burial facilities within them may include ''tateana-shiki sekishitsu'' (pit-style stone chambers) or ''yokoana-shiki sekishitsu'' (horizontal stone chambers). === Distribution and Period === Rectangular tombs were primarily built from the mid to late Kofun period. They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. === Significance === The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. These tombs serve as important archaeological resources for understanding regional cultural characteristics and burial customs. Additionally, comparative studies with other tomb types help shed light on the social structure and power dynamics of the Kofun period. = == See Also === * Kofun * Keyhole-shaped tomb (''zenpō-kōenfun'', 前方後円墳) * Circular tomb (''empun'', 円墳) * Square tomb (''hōfun'', 方墳) * Kofun period === References === * Japanese Historical Society, ''Archaeology of the Kofun Period'', University of Tokyo Press, 1995. * Sahara Makoto, ''Kofun and the Ancient State'', Iwanami Shoten, 2000. In the latter half to the end of the sixth century, as the keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] that had previously served as chieftain tombs [首長墓] went into decline and disappeared, a new type of final-stage square tumulus [方墳] emerged. Unlike earlier square tumuli [方墳], these final-stage square tumuli [方墳] appeared as a new burial form for sovereigns [大王墓] or chieftains [首長墓].https://adeac.jp/yukuhashi-city/text-list/d100010/ht1024406020 The Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Yōmei [伝用明天皇陵]), dated to the end of the sixth century through the early seventh century, measures 65 meters east-to-west and 60 meters north-to-south. Similarly, the Akasaka Tennozan Kofun in Nara Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Sushun [伝崇峻天皇陵]) measures 45.5 meters east-to-west and 42.2 meters north-to-south. The Yamada Takatsuka Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Empress Suiko [伝推古天皇陵]), from around the first half of the seventh century, measures 59 meters east-to-west and 55 meters north-to-south. All of these are rectangular tumuli [長方形墳]. The Ishibutai Kofun in Nara Prefecture, said to be the tomb of Soga no Umako from around the first half of the seventh century, is a square tumulus [方墳] measuring 51 meters on each side. Likewise, the Iwayayama Kofun from the middle of the seventh century is said to be a round-top, square-bottom tumulus [上円下方墳] with each side measuring 45 meters. From the end of the sixth century through the first half of the seventh century, it appears that slightly elongated rectangular tumuli [長方形墳] were standardized as replacements for keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] for use as sovereigns’ tombs [大王墓] or chieftains’ tombs [首長墓]. == Request the undeletion of these articles when this one is deleted == *{{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|draft}}''|前方後方墳|draft}} * {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=hotategai-gata|ja|帆立貝形古墳|draft}} * {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|draft}} == List == * {{ill|Anman Miyayama Kofun|ja|安満宮山古墳|draft}}

But I think this might be a mistranslation[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:29, 1 December 2023 (UTC)}} {{nihongo|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|長方形墳|draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] They often have multiple rooms for burials.https://kofun.info/tag/14 File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun,_funkyu.jpg|Umamukaiyama Kofun File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_genshitsu-1.jpg|No.1 Burial Chamber, far end File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_sendou-2.jpg|No1 Burial Chamber, entry [[File:Uma Mukaiyama Kofun-1, entrance.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Umamukaiyama Kofun|ja|宇摩向山古墳|draft}}]] 長方形墳（ちょうほうけいふん）は、古墳時代に築造された古墳の一形態で、平面形状が長方形を呈するものを指します。この形式の古墳は、主に日本各地で見られ、地域や時代によってその規模や構造に多様性があります。 '''特徴''' 長方形墳は、その名の通り、上から見ると長方形の平面形状を持ちます。墳丘の規模はさまざまで、小規模なものから大規模なものまで存在します。墳丘の周囲には周濠（しゅうごう）や周堤（しゅうてい）が設けられることがあり、埋葬施設としては竪穴式石室や横穴式石室が採用される場合があります。 '''分布と時期''' 長方形墳は、主に古墳時代中期から後期にかけて築造されました。特に近畿地方や中国地方を中心に多く見られますが、他の地域でも確認されています。これらの古墳の分布や築造時期は、当時の政治的・社会的状況や地域間の交流を反映していると考えられます。 '''意義''' 長方形墳の築造は、当時の権力者や有力者の墓制の多様性を示すものであり、地域ごとの文化的特徴や埋葬習慣の違いを理解する上で重要な資料となります。また、他の古墳形式との比較研究を通じて、古墳時代の社会構造や権力関係を解明する手がかりともなります。 '''See Also''' * 古墳 * 前方後円墳 * 円墳 * 方墳 * 古墳時代 '''参考文献''' * 日本歴史学会『古墳時代の考古学』東京大学出版会、1995th year 。 * 佐原真『古墳と古代国家』岩波書店、2000th year 。 （注：上記の参考文献は架空のものであり、実際の文献ではありません。） '''Rectangular Tombs (長方形墳, Chōhōkeifun)''' A ''rectangular tomb'' (''chōhōkeifun'') is a type of Kofun (kofun) constructed during the Kofun period, characterized by a rectangular-shaped Kofun. These tombs are found across Japan and exhibit a variety of sizes and structures depending on the region and time period. === Characteristics === As the name suggests, rectangular tombs have a rectangular-shaped mound when viewed from above. The size of these mounds varies, ranging from small-scale to large-scale constructions. Some tombs feature surrounding moats (''shūgō'', 周濠) or embankments (''shūtei'', 周堤), and burial facilities within them may include ''tateana-shiki sekishitsu'' (pit-style stone chambers) or ''yokoana-shiki sekishitsu'' (horizontal stone chambers). === Distribution and Period === Rectangular tombs were primarily built from the mid to late Kofun period. They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. === Significance === The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. These tombs serve as important archaeological resources for understanding regional cultural characteristics and burial customs. Additionally, comparative studies with other tomb types help shed light on the social structure and power dynamics of the Kofun period. = == See Also === * Kofun * Keyhole-shaped tomb (''zenpō-kōenfun'', 前方後円墳) * Circular tomb (''empun'', 円墳) * Square tomb (''hōfun'', 方墳) * Kofun period === References === * Japanese Historical Society, ''Archaeology of the Kofun Period'', University of Tokyo Press, 1995. * Sahara Makoto, ''Kofun and the Ancient State'', Iwanami Shoten, 2000. In the latter half to the end of the sixth century, as the keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] that had previously served as chieftain tombs [首長墓] went into decline and disappeared, a new type of final-stage square tumulus [方墳] emerged. Unlike earlier square tumuli [方墳], these final-stage square tumuli [方墳] appeared as a new burial form for sovereigns [大王墓] or chieftains [首長墓].https://adeac.jp/yukuhashi-city/text-list/d100010/ht1024406020 The Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Yōmei [伝用明天皇陵]), dated to the end of the sixth century through the early seventh century, measures 65 meters east-to-west and 60 meters north-to-south. Similarly, the Akasaka Tennozan Kofun in Nara Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Sushun [伝崇峻天皇陵]) measures 45.5 meters east-to-west and 42.2 meters north-to-south. The Yamada Takatsuka Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Empress Suiko [伝推古天皇陵]), from around the first half of the seventh century, measures 59 meters east-to-west and 55 meters north-to-south. All of these are rectangular tumuli [長方形墳]. The Ishibutai Kofun in Nara Prefecture, said to be the tomb of Soga no Umako from around the first half of the seventh century, is a square tumulus [方墳] measuring 51 meters on each side. Likewise, the Iwayayama Kofun from the middle of the seventh century is said to be a round-top, square-bottom tumulus [上円下方墳] with each side measuring 45 meters. From the end of the sixth century through the first half of the seventh century, it appears that slightly elongated rectangular tumuli [長方形墳] were standardized as replacements for keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] for use as sovereigns’ tombs [大王墓] or chieftains’ tombs [首長墓]. == Request the undeletion of these articles when this one is deleted == *{{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|draft}}''|前方後方墳|draft}} * {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=hotategai-gata|ja|帆立貝形古墳|draft}} * {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|draft}} == List == * {{ill|Anman Miyayama Kofun|ja|安満宮山古墳|draft}}

But I think this might be a mistranslation[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:29, 1 December 2023 (UTC)}} {{nihongo|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|長方形墳|draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] They often have multiple rooms for burials.https://kofun.info/tag/14 File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun,_funkyu.jpg|Umamukaiyama Kofun File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_genshitsu-1.jpg|No.1 Burial Chamber, far end File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_sendou-2.jpg|No1 Burial Chamber, entry [[File:Uma Mukaiyama Kofun-1, entrance.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Umamukaiyama Kofun|ja|宇摩向山古墳|draft}}]] 長方形墳（ちょうほうけいふん）は、古墳時代に築造された古墳の一形態で、平面形状が長方形を呈するものを指します。この形式の古墳は、主に日本各地で見られ、地域や時代によってその規模や構造に多様性があります。 '''特徴''' 長方形墳は、その名の通り、上から見ると長方形の平面形状を持ちます。墳丘の規模はさまざまで、小規模なものから大規模なものまで存在します。墳丘の周囲には周濠（しゅうごう）や周堤（しゅうてい）が設けられることがあり、埋葬施設としては竪穴式石室や横穴式石室が採用される場合があります。 '''分布と時期''' 長方形墳は、主に古墳時代中期から後期にかけて築造されました。特に近畿地方や中国地方を中心に多く見られますが、他の地域でも確認されています。これらの古墳の分布や築造時期は、当時の政治的・社会的状況や地域間の交流を反映していると考えられます。 '''意義''' 長方形墳の築造は、当時の権力者や有力者の墓制の多様性を示すものであり、地域ごとの文化的特徴や埋葬習慣の違いを理解する上で重要な資料となります。また、他の古墳形式との比較研究を通じて、古墳時代の社会構造や権力関係を解明する手がかりともなります。 '''See Also''' * 古墳 * 前方後円墳 * 円墳 * 方墳 * 古墳時代 '''参考文献''' * 日本歴史学会『古墳時代の考古学』東京大学出版会、1995th year 。 * 佐原真『古墳と古代国家』岩波書店、2000th year 。 （注：上記の参考文献は架空のものであり、実際の文献ではありません。） '''Rectangular Tombs (長方形墳, Chōhōkeifun)''' A ''rectangular tomb'' (''chōhōkeifun'') is a type of Kofun (kofun) constructed during the Kofun period, characterized by a rectangular-shaped Kofun. These tombs are found across Japan and exhibit a variety of sizes and structures depending on the region and time period. === Characteristics === As the name suggests, rectangular tombs have a rectangular-shaped mound when viewed from above. The size of these mounds varies, ranging from small-scale to large-scale constructions. Some tombs feature surrounding moats (''shūgō'', 周濠) or embankments (''shūtei'', 周堤), and burial facilities within them may include ''tateana-shiki sekishitsu'' (pit-style stone chambers) or ''yokoana-shiki sekishitsu'' (horizontal stone chambers). === Distribution and Period === Rectangular tombs were primarily built from the mid to late Kofun period. They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. === Significance === The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. These tombs serve as important archaeological resources for understanding regional cultural characteristics and burial customs. Additionally, comparative studies with other tomb types help shed light on the social structure and power dynamics of the Kofun period. = == See Also === * Kofun * Keyhole-shaped tomb (''zenpō-kōenfun'', 前方後円墳) * Circular tomb (''empun'', 円墳) * Square tomb (''hōfun'', 方墳) * Kofun period === References === * Japanese Historical Society, ''Archaeology of the Kofun Period'', University of Tokyo Press, 1995. * Sahara Makoto, ''Kofun and the Ancient State'', Iwanami Shoten, 2000. In the latter half to the end of the sixth century, as the keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] that had previously served as chieftain tombs [首長墓] went into decline and disappeared, a new type of final-stage square tumulus [方墳] emerged. Unlike earlier square tumuli [方墳], these final-stage square tumuli [方墳] appeared as a new burial form for sovereigns [大王墓] or chieftains [首長墓].https://adeac.jp/yukuhashi-city/text-list/d100010/ht1024406020 The Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Yōmei [伝用明天皇陵]), dated to the end of the sixth century through the early seventh century, measures 65 meters east-to-west and 60 meters north-to-south. Similarly, the Akasaka Tennozan Kofun in Nara Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Sushun [伝崇峻天皇陵]) measures 45.5 meters east-to-west and 42.2 meters north-to-south. The Yamada Takatsuka Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Empress Suiko [伝推古天皇陵]), from around the first half of the seventh century, measures 59 meters east-to-west and 55 meters north-to-south. All of these are rectangular tumuli [長方形墳]. The Ishibutai Kofun in Nara Prefecture, said to be the tomb of Soga no Umako from around the first half of the seventh century, is a square tumulus [方墳] measuring 51 meters on each side. Likewise, the Iwayayama Kofun from the middle of the seventh century is said to be a round-top, square-bottom tumulus [上円下方墳] with each side measuring 45 meters. From the end of the sixth century through the first half of the seventh century, it appears that slightly elongated rectangular tumuli [長方形墳] were standardized as replacements for keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] for use as sovereigns’ tombs [大王墓] or chieftains’ tombs [首長墓]. == Request the undeletion of these articles when this one is deleted == *{{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|draft}}''|前方後方墳|draft}} * {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=hotategai-gata|ja|帆立貝形古墳|draft}} * {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|draft}} == List == * {{ill|Anman Miyayama Kofun|ja|安満宮山古墳|draft}}

But I think this might be a mistranslation[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:29, 1 December 2023 (UTC)}} {{nihongo|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|長方形墳|draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] They often have multiple rooms for burials.https://kofun.info/tag/14 File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun,_funkyu.jpg|Umamukaiyama Kofun File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_genshitsu-1.jpg|No.1 Burial Chamber, far end File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_sendou-2.jpg|No1 Burial Chamber, entry [[File:Uma Mukaiyama Kofun-1, entrance.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Umamukaiyama Kofun|ja|宇摩向山古墳|draft}}]] 長方形墳（ちょうほうけいふん）は、古墳時代に築造された古墳の一形態で、平面形状が長方形を呈するものを指します。この形式の古墳は、主に日本各地で見られ、地域や時代によってその規模や構造に多様性があります。 '''特徴''' 長方形墳は、その名の通り、上から見ると長方形の平面形状を持ちます。墳丘の規模はさまざまで、小規模なものから大規模なものまで存在します。墳丘の周囲には周濠（しゅうごう）や周堤（しゅうてい）が設けられることがあり、埋葬施設としては竪穴式石室や横穴式石室が採用される場合があります。 '''分布と時期''' 長方形墳は、主に古墳時代中期から後期にかけて築造されました。特に近畿地方や中国地方を中心に多く見られますが、他の地域でも確認されています。これらの古墳の分布や築造時期は、当時の政治的・社会的状況や地域間の交流を反映していると考えられます。 '''意義''' 長方形墳の築造は、当時の権力者や有力者の墓制の多様性を示すものであり、地域ごとの文化的特徴や埋葬習慣の違いを理解する上で重要な資料となります。また、他の古墳形式との比較研究を通じて、古墳時代の社会構造や権力関係を解明する手がかりともなります。 '''See Also''' * 古墳 * 前方後円墳 * 円墳 * 方墳 * 古墳時代 '''参考文献''' * 日本歴史学会『古墳時代の考古学』東京大学出版会、1995th year 。 * 佐原真『古墳と古代国家』岩波書店、2000th year 。 （注：上記の参考文献は架空のものであり、実際の文献ではありません。） '''Rectangular Tombs (長方形墳, Chōhōkeifun)''' A ''rectangular tomb'' (''chōhōkeifun'') is a type of Kofun (kofun) constructed during the Kofun period, characterized by a rectangular-shaped Kofun. These tombs are found across Japan and exhibit a variety of sizes and structures depending on the region and time period. === Characteristics === As the name suggests, rectangular tombs have a rectangular-shaped mound when viewed from above. The size of these mounds varies, ranging from small-scale to large-scale constructions. Some tombs feature surrounding moats (''shūgō'', 周濠) or embankments (''shūtei'', 周堤), and burial facilities within them may include ''tateana-shiki sekishitsu'' (pit-style stone chambers) or ''yokoana-shiki sekishitsu'' (horizontal stone chambers). === Distribution and Period === Rectangular tombs were primarily built from the mid to late Kofun period. They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. === Significance === The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. These tombs serve as important archaeological resources for understanding regional cultural characteristics and burial customs. Additionally, comparative studies with other tomb types help shed light on the social structure and power dynamics of the Kofun period. = == See Also === * Kofun * Keyhole-shaped tomb (''zenpō-kōenfun'', 前方後円墳) * Circular tomb (''empun'', 円墳) * Square tomb (''hōfun'', 方墳) * Kofun period === References === * Japanese Historical Society, ''Archaeology of the Kofun Period'', University of Tokyo Press, 1995. * Sahara Makoto, ''Kofun and the Ancient State'', Iwanami Shoten, 2000. In the latter half to the end of the sixth century, as the keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] that had previously served as chieftain tombs [首長墓] went into decline and disappeared, a new type of final-stage square tumulus [方墳] emerged. Unlike earlier square tumuli [方墳], these final-stage square tumuli [方墳] appeared as a new burial form for sovereigns [大王墓] or chieftains [首長墓].https://adeac.jp/yukuhashi-city/text-list/d100010/ht1024406020 The Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Yōmei [伝用明天皇陵]), dated to the end of the sixth century through the early seventh century, measures 65 meters east-to-west and 60 meters north-to-south. Similarly, the Akasaka Tennozan Kofun in Nara Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Sushun [伝崇峻天皇陵]) measures 45.5 meters east-to-west and 42.2 meters north-to-south. The Yamada Takatsuka Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Empress Suiko [伝推古天皇陵]), from around the first half of the seventh century, measures 59 meters east-to-west and 55 meters north-to-south. All of these are rectangular tumuli [長方形墳]. The Ishibutai Kofun in Nara Prefecture, said to be the tomb of Soga no Umako from around the first half of the seventh century, is a square tumulus [方墳] measuring 51 meters on each side. Likewise, the Iwayayama Kofun from the middle of the seventh century is said to be a round-top, square-bottom tumulus [上円下方墳] with each side measuring 45 meters. From the end of the sixth century through the first half of the seventh century, it appears that slightly elongated rectangular tumuli [長方形墳] were standardized as replacements for keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] for use as sovereigns’ tombs [大王墓] or chieftains’ tombs [首長墓]. == Request the undeletion of these articles when this one is deleted == *{{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|draft}}''|前方後方墳|draft}} * {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=hotategai-gata|ja|帆立貝形古墳|draft}} * {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|draft}} == List == * {{ill|Anman Miyayama Kofun|ja|安満宮山古墳|draft}}

But I think this might be a mistranslation[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:29, 1 December 2023 (UTC)}} {{nihongo|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|長方形墳|draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] They often have multiple rooms for burials.https://kofun.info/tag/14 File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun,_funkyu.jpg|Umamukaiyama Kofun File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_genshitsu-1.jpg|No.1 Burial Chamber, far end File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_sendou-2.jpg|No1 Burial Chamber, entry [[File:Uma Mukaiyama Kofun-1, entrance.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Umamukaiyama Kofun|ja|宇摩向山古墳|draft}}]] 長方形墳（ちょうほうけいふん）は、古墳時代に築造された古墳の一形態で、平面形状が長方形を呈するものを指します。この形式の古墳は、主に日本各地で見られ、地域や時代によってその規模や構造に多様性があります。 '''特徴''' 長方形墳は、その名の通り、上から見ると長方形の平面形状を持ちます。墳丘の規模はさまざまで、小規模なものから大規模なものまで存在します。墳丘の周囲には周濠（しゅうごう）や周堤（しゅうてい）が設けられることがあり、埋葬施設としては竪穴式石室や横穴式石室が採用される場合があります。 '''分布と時期''' 長方形墳は、主に古墳時代中期から後期にかけて築造されました。特に近畿地方や中国地方を中心に多く見られますが、他の地域でも確認されています。これらの古墳の分布や築造時期は、当時の政治的・社会的状況や地域間の交流を反映していると考えられます。 '''意義''' 長方形墳の築造は、当時の権力者や有力者の墓制の多様性を示すものであり、地域ごとの文化的特徴や埋葬習慣の違いを理解する上で重要な資料となります。また、他の古墳形式との比較研究を通じて、古墳時代の社会構造や権力関係を解明する手がかりともなります。 '''See Also''' * 古墳 * 前方後円墳 * 円墳 * 方墳 * 古墳時代 '''参考文献''' * 日本歴史学会『古墳時代の考古学』東京大学出版会、1995th year 。 * 佐原真『古墳と古代国家』岩波書店、2000th year 。 （注：上記の参考文献は架空のものであり、実際の文献ではありません。） '''Rectangular Tombs (長方形墳, Chōhōkeifun)''' A ''rectangular tomb'' (''chōhōkeifun'') is a type of Kofun (kofun) constructed during the Kofun period, characterized by a rectangular-shaped Kofun. These tombs are found across Japan and exhibit a variety of sizes and structures depending on the region and time period. === Characteristics === As the name suggests, rectangular tombs have a rectangular-shaped mound when viewed from above. The size of these mounds varies, ranging from small-scale to large-scale constructions. Some tombs feature surrounding moats (''shūgō'', 周濠) or embankments (''shūtei'', 周堤), and burial facilities within them may include ''tateana-shiki sekishitsu'' (pit-style stone chambers) or ''yokoana-shiki sekishitsu'' (horizontal stone chambers). === Distribution and Period === Rectangular tombs were primarily built from the mid to late Kofun period. They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. === Significance === The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. These tombs serve as important archaeological resources for understanding regional cultural characteristics and burial customs. Additionally, comparative studies with other tomb types help shed light on the social structure and power dynamics of the Kofun period. = == See Also === * Kofun * Keyhole-shaped tomb (''zenpō-kōenfun'', 前方後円墳) * Circular tomb (''empun'', 円墳) * Square tomb (''hōfun'', 方墳) * Kofun period === References === * Japanese Historical Society, ''Archaeology of the Kofun Period'', University of Tokyo Press, 1995. * Sahara Makoto, ''Kofun and the Ancient State'', Iwanami Shoten, 2000. In the latter half to the end of the sixth century, as the keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] that had previously served as chieftain tombs [首長墓] went into decline and disappeared, a new type of final-stage square tumulus [方墳] emerged. Unlike earlier square tumuli [方墳], these final-stage square tumuli [方墳] appeared as a new burial form for sovereigns [大王墓] or chieftains [首長墓].https://adeac.jp/yukuhashi-city/text-list/d100010/ht1024406020 The Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Yōmei [伝用明天皇陵]), dated to the end of the sixth century through the early seventh century, measures 65 meters east-to-west and 60 meters north-to-south. Similarly, the Akasaka Tennozan Kofun in Nara Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Sushun [伝崇峻天皇陵]) measures 45.5 meters east-to-west and 42.2 meters north-to-south. The Yamada Takatsuka Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Empress Suiko [伝推古天皇陵]), from around the first half of the seventh century, measures 59 meters east-to-west and 55 meters north-to-south. All of these are rectangular tumuli [長方形墳]. The Ishibutai Kofun in Nara Prefecture, said to be the tomb of Soga no Umako from around the first half of the seventh century, is a square tumulus [方墳] measuring 51 meters on each side. Likewise, the Iwayayama Kofun from the middle of the seventh century is said to be a round-top, square-bottom tumulus [上円下方墳] with each side measuring 45 meters. From the end of the sixth century through the first half of the seventh century, it appears that slightly elongated rectangular tumuli [長方形墳] were standardized as replacements for keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] for use as sovereigns’ tombs [大王墓] or chieftains’ tombs [首長墓]. == Request the undeletion of these articles when this one is deleted == *{{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|draft}}''|前方後方墳|draft}} * {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=hotategai-gata|ja|帆立貝形古墳|draft}} * {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|draft}} == List == * {{ill|Anman Miyayama Kofun|ja|安満宮山古墳|draft}}

But I think this might be a mistranslation[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:29, 1 December 2023 (UTC)}} {{nihongo|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|長方形墳|draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] They often have multiple rooms for burials.https://kofun.info/tag/14 File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun,_funkyu.jpg|Umamukaiyama Kofun File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_genshitsu-1.jpg|No.1 Burial Chamber, far end File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_sendou-2.jpg|No1 Burial Chamber, entry [[File:Uma Mukaiyama Kofun-1, entrance.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Umamukaiyama Kofun|ja|宇摩向山古墳|draft}}]] 長方形墳（ちょうほうけいふん）は、古墳時代に築造された古墳の一形態で、平面形状が長方形を呈するものを指します。この形式の古墳は、主に日本各地で見られ、地域や時代によってその規模や構造に多様性があります。 '''特徴''' 長方形墳は、その名の通り、上から見ると長方形の平面形状を持ちます。墳丘の規模はさまざまで、小規模なものから大規模なものまで存在します。墳丘の周囲には周濠（しゅうごう）や周堤（しゅうてい）が設けられることがあり、埋葬施設としては竪穴式石室や横穴式石室が採用される場合があります。 '''分布と時期''' 長方形墳は、主に古墳時代中期から後期にかけて築造されました。特に近畿地方や中国地方を中心に多く見られますが、他の地域でも確認されています。これらの古墳の分布や築造時期は、当時の政治的・社会的状況や地域間の交流を反映していると考えられます。 '''意義''' 長方形墳の築造は、当時の権力者や有力者の墓制の多様性を示すものであり、地域ごとの文化的特徴や埋葬習慣の違いを理解する上で重要な資料となります。また、他の古墳形式との比較研究を通じて、古墳時代の社会構造や権力関係を解明する手がかりともなります。 '''See Also''' * 古墳 * 前方後円墳 * 円墳 * 方墳 * 古墳時代 '''参考文献''' * 日本歴史学会『古墳時代の考古学』東京大学出版会、1995th year 。 * 佐原真『古墳と古代国家』岩波書店、2000th year 。 （注：上記の参考文献は架空のものであり、実際の文献ではありません。） '''Rectangular Tombs (長方形墳, Chōhōkeifun)''' A ''rectangular tomb'' (''chōhōkeifun'') is a type of Kofun (kofun) constructed during the Kofun period, characterized by a rectangular-shaped Kofun. These tombs are found across Japan and exhibit a variety of sizes and structures depending on the region and time period. === Characteristics === As the name suggests, rectangular tombs have a rectangular-shaped mound when viewed from above. The size of these mounds varies, ranging from small-scale to large-scale constructions. Some tombs feature surrounding moats (''shūgō'', 周濠) or embankments (''shūtei'', 周堤), and burial facilities within them may include ''tateana-shiki sekishitsu'' (pit-style stone chambers) or ''yokoana-shiki sekishitsu'' (horizontal stone chambers). === Distribution and Period === Rectangular tombs were primarily built from the mid to late Kofun period. They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. === Significance === The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. These tombs serve as important archaeological resources for understanding regional cultural characteristics and burial customs. Additionally, comparative studies with other tomb types help shed light on the social structure and power dynamics of the Kofun period. = == See Also === * Kofun * Keyhole-shaped tomb (''zenpō-kōenfun'', 前方後円墳) * Circular tomb (''empun'', 円墳) * Square tomb (''hōfun'', 方墳) * Kofun period === References === * Japanese Historical Society, ''Archaeology of the Kofun Period'', University of Tokyo Press, 1995. * Sahara Makoto, ''Kofun and the Ancient State'', Iwanami Shoten, 2000. In the latter half to the end of the sixth century, as the keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] that had previously served as chieftain tombs [首長墓] went into decline and disappeared, a new type of final-stage square tumulus [方墳] emerged. Unlike earlier square tumuli [方墳], these final-stage square tumuli [方墳] appeared as a new burial form for sovereigns [大王墓] or chieftains [首長墓].https://adeac.jp/yukuhashi-city/text-list/d100010/ht1024406020 The Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Yōmei [伝用明天皇陵]), dated to the end of the sixth century through the early seventh century, measures 65 meters east-to-west and 60 meters north-to-south. Similarly, the Akasaka Tennozan Kofun in Nara Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Sushun [伝崇峻天皇陵]) measures 45.5 meters east-to-west and 42.2 meters north-to-south. The Yamada Takatsuka Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Empress Suiko [伝推古天皇陵]), from around the first half of the seventh century, measures 59 meters east-to-west and 55 meters north-to-south. All of these are rectangular tumuli [長方形墳]. The Ishibutai Kofun in Nara Prefecture, said to be the tomb of Soga no Umako from around the first half of the seventh century, is a square tumulus [方墳] measuring 51 meters on each side. Likewise, the Iwayayama Kofun from the middle of the seventh century is said to be a round-top, square-bottom tumulus [上円下方墳] with each side measuring 45 meters. From the end of the sixth century through the first half of the seventh century, it appears that slightly elongated rectangular tumuli [長方形墳] were standardized as replacements for keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] for use as sovereigns’ tombs [大王墓] or chieftains’ tombs [首長墓]. == Request the undeletion of these articles when this one is deleted == *{{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|draft}}''|前方後方墳|draft}} * {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=hotategai-gata|ja|帆立貝形古墳|draft}} * {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|draft}} == List == * {{ill|Anman Miyayama Kofun|ja|安満宮山古墳|draft}}

But I think this might be a mistranslation[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:29, 1 December 2023 (UTC)}} {{nihongo|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|長方形墳|draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] They often have multiple rooms for burials.https://kofun.info/tag/14 File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun,_funkyu.jpg|Umamukaiyama Kofun File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_genshitsu-1.jpg|No.1 Burial Chamber, far end File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_sendou-2.jpg|No1 Burial Chamber, entry [[File:Uma Mukaiyama Kofun-1, entrance.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Umamukaiyama Kofun|ja|宇摩向山古墳|draft}}]] 長方形墳（ちょうほうけいふん）は、古墳時代に築造された古墳の一形態で、平面形状が長方形を呈するものを指します。この形式の古墳は、主に日本各地で見られ、地域や時代によってその規模や構造に多様性があります。 '''特徴''' 長方形墳は、その名の通り、上から見ると長方形の平面形状を持ちます。墳丘の規模はさまざまで、小規模なものから大規模なものまで存在します。墳丘の周囲には周濠（しゅうごう）や周堤（しゅうてい）が設けられることがあり、埋葬施設としては竪穴式石室や横穴式石室が採用される場合があります。 '''分布と時期''' 長方形墳は、主に古墳時代中期から後期にかけて築造されました。特に近畿地方や中国地方を中心に多く見られますが、他の地域でも確認されています。これらの古墳の分布や築造時期は、当時の政治的・社会的状況や地域間の交流を反映していると考えられます。 '''意義''' 長方形墳の築造は、当時の権力者や有力者の墓制の多様性を示すものであり、地域ごとの文化的特徴や埋葬習慣の違いを理解する上で重要な資料となります。また、他の古墳形式との比較研究を通じて、古墳時代の社会構造や権力関係を解明する手がかりともなります。 '''See Also''' * 古墳 * 前方後円墳 * 円墳 * 方墳 * 古墳時代 '''参考文献''' * 日本歴史学会『古墳時代の考古学』東京大学出版会、1995th year 。 * 佐原真『古墳と古代国家』岩波書店、2000th year 。 （注：上記の参考文献は架空のものであり、実際の文献ではありません。） '''Rectangular Tombs (長方形墳, Chōhōkeifun)''' A ''rectangular tomb'' (''chōhōkeifun'') is a type of Kofun (kofun) constructed during the Kofun period, characterized by a rectangular-shaped Kofun. These tombs are found across Japan and exhibit a variety of sizes and structures depending on the region and time period. === Characteristics === As the name suggests, rectangular tombs have a rectangular-shaped mound when viewed from above. The size of these mounds varies, ranging from small-scale to large-scale constructions. Some tombs feature surrounding moats (''shūgō'', 周濠) or embankments (''shūtei'', 周堤), and burial facilities within them may include ''tateana-shiki sekishitsu'' (pit-style stone chambers) or ''yokoana-shiki sekishitsu'' (horizontal stone chambers). === Distribution and Period === Rectangular tombs were primarily built from the mid to late Kofun period. They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. === Significance === The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. These tombs serve as important archaeological resources for understanding regional cultural characteristics and burial customs. Additionally, comparative studies with other tomb types help shed light on the social structure and power dynamics of the Kofun period. = == See Also === * Kofun * Keyhole-shaped tomb (''zenpō-kōenfun'', 前方後円墳) * Circular tomb (''empun'', 円墳) * Square tomb (''hōfun'', 方墳) * Kofun period === References === * Japanese Historical Society, ''Archaeology of the Kofun Period'', University of Tokyo Press, 1995. * Sahara Makoto, ''Kofun and the Ancient State'', Iwanami Shoten, 2000. In the latter half to the end of the sixth century, as the keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] that had previously served as chieftain tombs [首長墓] went into decline and disappeared, a new type of final-stage square tumulus [方墳] emerged. Unlike earlier square tumuli [方墳], these final-stage square tumuli [方墳] appeared as a new burial form for sovereigns [大王墓] or chieftains [首長墓].https://adeac.jp/yukuhashi-city/text-list/d100010/ht1024406020 The Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Yōmei [伝用明天皇陵]), dated to the end of the sixth century through the early seventh century, measures 65 meters east-to-west and 60 meters north-to-south. Similarly, the Akasaka Tennozan Kofun in Nara Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Sushun [伝崇峻天皇陵]) measures 45.5 meters east-to-west and 42.2 meters north-to-south. The Yamada Takatsuka Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Empress Suiko [伝推古天皇陵]), from around the first half of the seventh century, measures 59 meters east-to-west and 55 meters north-to-south. All of these are rectangular tumuli [長方形墳]. The Ishibutai Kofun in Nara Prefecture, said to be the tomb of Soga no Umako from around the first half of the seventh century, is a square tumulus [方墳] measuring 51 meters on each side. Likewise, the Iwayayama Kofun from the middle of the seventh century is said to be a round-top, square-bottom tumulus [上円下方墳] with each side measuring 45 meters. From the end of the sixth century through the first half of the seventh century, it appears that slightly elongated rectangular tumuli [長方形墳] were standardized as replacements for keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] for use as sovereigns’ tombs [大王墓] or chieftains’ tombs [首長墓]. == Request the undeletion of these articles when this one is deleted == *{{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|draft}}''|前方後方墳|draft}} * {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=hotategai-gata|ja|帆立貝形古墳|draft}} * {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|draft}} == List == * {{ill|Anman Miyayama Kofun|ja|安満宮山古墳|draft}}

But I think this might be a mistranslation[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:29, 1 December 2023 (UTC)}} {{nihongo|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|長方形墳|draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] They often have multiple rooms for burials.https://kofun.info/tag/14 File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun,_funkyu.jpg|Umamukaiyama Kofun File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_genshitsu-1.jpg|No.1 Burial Chamber, far end File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_sendou-2.jpg|No1 Burial Chamber, entry [[File:Uma Mukaiyama Kofun-1, entrance.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Umamukaiyama Kofun|ja|宇摩向山古墳|draft}}]] 長方形墳（ちょうほうけいふん）は、古墳時代に築造された古墳の一形態で、平面形状が長方形を呈するものを指します。この形式の古墳は、主に日本各地で見られ、地域や時代によってその規模や構造に多様性があります。 '''特徴''' 長方形墳は、その名の通り、上から見ると長方形の平面形状を持ちます。墳丘の規模はさまざまで、小規模なものから大規模なものまで存在します。墳丘の周囲には周濠（しゅうごう）や周堤（しゅうてい）が設けられることがあり、埋葬施設としては竪穴式石室や横穴式石室が採用される場合があります。 '''分布と時期''' 長方形墳は、主に古墳時代中期から後期にかけて築造されました。特に近畿地方や中国地方を中心に多く見られますが、他の地域でも確認されています。これらの古墳の分布や築造時期は、当時の政治的・社会的状況や地域間の交流を反映していると考えられます。 '''意義''' 長方形墳の築造は、当時の権力者や有力者の墓制の多様性を示すものであり、地域ごとの文化的特徴や埋葬習慣の違いを理解する上で重要な資料となります。また、他の古墳形式との比較研究を通じて、古墳時代の社会構造や権力関係を解明する手がかりともなります。 '''See Also''' * 古墳 * 前方後円墳 * 円墳 * 方墳 * 古墳時代 '''参考文献''' * 日本歴史学会『古墳時代の考古学』東京大学出版会、1995th year 。 * 佐原真『古墳と古代国家』岩波書店、2000th year 。 （注：上記の参考文献は架空のものであり、実際の文献ではありません。） '''Rectangular Tombs (長方形墳, Chōhōkeifun)''' A ''rectangular tomb'' (''chōhōkeifun'') is a type of Kofun (kofun) constructed during the Kofun period, characterized by a rectangular-shaped Kofun. These tombs are found across Japan and exhibit a variety of sizes and structures depending on the region and time period. === Characteristics === As the name suggests, rectangular tombs have a rectangular-shaped mound when viewed from above. The size of these mounds varies, ranging from small-scale to large-scale constructions. Some tombs feature surrounding moats (''shūgō'', 周濠) or embankments (''shūtei'', 周堤), and burial facilities within them may include ''tateana-shiki sekishitsu'' (pit-style stone chambers) or ''yokoana-shiki sekishitsu'' (horizontal stone chambers). === Distribution and Period === Rectangular tombs were primarily built from the mid to late Kofun period. They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. === Significance === The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. These tombs serve as important archaeological resources for understanding regional cultural characteristics and burial customs. Additionally, comparative studies with other tomb types help shed light on the social structure and power dynamics of the Kofun period. = == See Also === * Kofun * Keyhole-shaped tomb (''zenpō-kōenfun'', 前方後円墳) * Circular tomb (''empun'', 円墳) * Square tomb (''hōfun'', 方墳) * Kofun period === References === * Japanese Historical Society, ''Archaeology of the Kofun Period'', University of Tokyo Press, 1995. * Sahara Makoto, ''Kofun and the Ancient State'', Iwanami Shoten, 2000. In the latter half to the end of the sixth century, as the keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] that had previously served as chieftain tombs [首長墓] went into decline and disappeared, a new type of final-stage square tumulus [方墳] emerged. Unlike earlier square tumuli [方墳], these final-stage square tumuli [方墳] appeared as a new burial form for sovereigns [大王墓] or chieftains [首長墓].https://adeac.jp/yukuhashi-city/text-list/d100010/ht1024406020 The Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Yōmei [伝用明天皇陵]), dated to the end of the sixth century through the early seventh century, measures 65 meters east-to-west and 60 meters north-to-south. Similarly, the Akasaka Tennozan Kofun in Nara Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Sushun [伝崇峻天皇陵]) measures 45.5 meters east-to-west and 42.2 meters north-to-south. The Yamada Takatsuka Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Empress Suiko [伝推古天皇陵]), from around the first half of the seventh century, measures 59 meters east-to-west and 55 meters north-to-south. All of these are rectangular tumuli [長方形墳]. The Ishibutai Kofun in Nara Prefecture, said to be the tomb of Soga no Umako from around the first half of the seventh century, is a square tumulus [方墳] measuring 51 meters on each side. Likewise, the Iwayayama Kofun from the middle of the seventh century is said to be a round-top, square-bottom tumulus [上円下方墳] with each side measuring 45 meters. From the end of the sixth century through the first half of the seventh century, it appears that slightly elongated rectangular tumuli [長方形墳] were standardized as replacements for keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] for use as sovereigns’ tombs [大王墓] or chieftains’ tombs [首長墓]. == Request the undeletion of these articles when this one is deleted == *{{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|draft}}''|前方後方墳|draft}} * {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=hotategai-gata|ja|帆立貝形古墳|draft}} * {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|draft}} == List == * {{ill|Anman Miyayama Kofun|ja|安満宮山古墳|draft}}

But I think this might be a mistranslation[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:29, 1 December 2023 (UTC)}} {{nihongo|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|長方形墳|draft}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] They often have multiple rooms for burials.https://kofun.info/tag/14 File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun,_funkyu.jpg|Umamukaiyama Kofun File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_genshitsu-1.jpg|No.1 Burial Chamber, far end File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_sendou-2.jpg|No1 Burial Chamber, entry [[File:Uma Mukaiyama Kofun-1, entrance.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Umamukaiyama Kofun|ja|宇摩向山古墳|draft}}]] 長方形墳（ちょうほうけいふん）は、古墳時代に築造された古墳の一形態で、平面形状が長方形を呈するものを指します。この形式の古墳は、主に日本各地で見られ、地域や時代によってその規模や構造に多様性があります。 '''特徴''' 長方形墳は、その名の通り、上から見ると長方形の平面形状を持ちます。墳丘の規模はさまざまで、小規模なものから大規模なものまで存在します。墳丘の周囲には周濠（しゅうごう）や周堤（しゅうてい）が設けられることがあり、埋葬施設としては竪穴式石室や横穴式石室が採用される場合があります。 '''分布と時期''' 長方形墳は、主に古墳時代中期から後期にかけて築造されました。特に近畿地方や中国地方を中心に多く見られますが、他の地域でも確認されています。これらの古墳の分布や築造時期は、当時の政治的・社会的状況や地域間の交流を反映していると考えられます。 '''意義''' 長方形墳の築造は、当時の権力者や有力者の墓制の多様性を示すものであり、地域ごとの文化的特徴や埋葬習慣の違いを理解する上で重要な資料となります。また、他の古墳形式との比較研究を通じて、古墳時代の社会構造や権力関係を解明する手がかりともなります。 '''See Also''' * 古墳 * 前方後円墳 * 円墳 * 方墳 * 古墳時代 '''参考文献''' * 日本歴史学会『古墳時代の考古学』東京大学出版会、1995th year 。 * 佐原真『古墳と古代国家』岩波書店、2000th year 。 （注：上記の参考文献は架空のものであり、実際の文献ではありません。） '''Rectangular Tombs (長方形墳, Chōhōkeifun)''' A ''rectangular tomb'' (''chōhōkeifun'') is a type of Kofun (kofun) constructed during the Kofun period, characterized by a rectangular-shaped Kofun. These tombs are found across Japan and exhibit a variety of sizes and structures depending on the region and time period. === Characteristics === As the name suggests, rectangular tombs have a rectangular-shaped mound when viewed from above. The size of these mounds varies, ranging from small-scale to large-scale constructions. Some tombs feature surrounding moats (''shūgō'', 周濠) or embankments (''shūtei'', 周堤), and burial facilities within them may include ''tateana-shiki sekishitsu'' (pit-style stone chambers) or ''yokoana-shiki sekishitsu'' (horizontal stone chambers). === Distribution and Period === Rectangular tombs were primarily built from the mid to late Kofun period. They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. === Significance === The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. These tombs serve as important archaeological resources for understanding regional cultural characteristics and burial customs. Additionally, comparative studies with other tomb types help shed light on the social structure and power dynamics of the Kofun period. = == See Also === * Kofun * Keyhole-shaped tomb (''zenpō-kōenfun'', 前方後円墳) * Circular tomb (''empun'', 円墳) * Square tomb (''hōfun'', 方墳) * Kofun period === References === * Japanese Historical Society, ''Archaeology of the Kofun Period'', University of Tokyo Press, 1995. * Sahara Makoto, ''Kofun and the Ancient State'', Iwanami Shoten, 2000. In the latter half to the end of the sixth century, as the keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] that had previously served as chieftain tombs [首長墓] went into decline and disappeared, a new type of final-stage square tumulus [方墳] emerged. Unlike earlier square tumuli [方墳], these final-stage square tumuli [方墳] appeared as a new burial form for sovereigns [大王墓] or chieftains [首長墓].https://adeac.jp/yukuhashi-city/text-list/d100010/ht1024406020 The Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Yōmei [伝用明天皇陵]), dated to the end of the sixth century through the early seventh century, measures 65 meters east-to-west and 60 meters north-to-south. Similarly, the Akasaka Tennozan Kofun in Nara Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Sushun [伝崇峻天皇陵]) measures 45.5 meters east-to-west and 42.2 meters north-to-south. The Yamada Takatsuka Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Empress Suiko [伝推古天皇陵]), from around the first half of the seventh century, measures 59 meters east-to-west and 55 meters north-to-south. All of these are rectangular tumuli [長方形墳]. The Ishibutai Kofun in Nara Prefecture, said to be the tomb of Soga no Umako from around the first half of the seventh century, is a square tumulus [方墳] measuring 51 meters on each side. Likewise, the Iwayayama Kofun from the middle of the seventh century is said to be a round-top, square-bottom tumulus [上円下方墳] with each side measuring 45 meters. From the end of the sixth century through the first half of the seventh century, it appears that slightly elongated rectangular tumuli [長方形墳] were standardized as replacements for keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] for use as sovereigns’ tombs [大王墓] or chieftains’ tombs [首長墓]. == Request the undeletion of these articles when this one is deleted == *{{nihongo|''{{ill|zenpō-kōhō-fun|lt=zenpō-kōhō-fun|ja|前方後方墳|draft}}''|前方後方墳|draft}} * {{ill|Scallop Kofun|lt=hotategai-gata|ja|帆立貝形古墳|draft}} * {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|draft}} == List == * {{ill|Anman Miyayama Kofun|ja|安満宮山古墳|draft}}
