But I think this might be a mistranslation[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:29, 1 December 2023 (UTC)}} {{Afc comment|1=This is the one Kofun type that is not covered by Japanese wikipedia. It is unclear how notable it is but there is a Category[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 20:41, 23 October 2023 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=If this times out then delete the Category since the only mainspace member of the Category [[:en:Umamukaiyama Kofun|Umamukaiyama Kofun]] is also in the {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} Category[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:38, 23 October 2023 (UTC) – draft}} {{nihongo|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|長方形墳}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] They often have multiple rooms for burials.https://kofun.info/tag/14 File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun,_funkyu.jpg|Umamukaiyama Kofun File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_genshitsu-1.jpg|No.1 Burial Chamber, far end File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_sendou-2.jpg|No1 Burial Chamber, entry [[File:Uma Mukaiyama Kofun-1, entrance.jpg|thumb|[[:en:Umamukaiyama Kofun|Umamukaiyama Kofun]]]] '''Rectangular Tombs (長方形墳, Chōhōkeifun)''' A ''rectangular tomb'' (''chōhōkeifun'') is a type of Kofun (kofun) constructed during the Kofun period, characterized by a rectangular-shaped Kofun. These tombs are found across Japan and exhibit a variety of sizes and structures depending on the region and time period. === Characteristics === As the name suggests, rectangular tombs have a rectangular-shaped mound when viewed from above. The size of these mounds varies, ranging from small-scale to large-scale constructions. Some tombs feature surrounding moats (''shūgō'', 周濠) or embankments (''shūtei'', 周堤), and burial facilities within them may include ''tateana-shiki sekishitsu'' (pit-style stone chambers) or ''yokoana-shiki sekishitsu'' (horizontal stone chambers). === Distribution and Period === Rectangular tombs were primarily built from the mid to late Kofun period. They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. === Significance === The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. These tombs serve as important archaeological resources for understanding regional cultural characteristics and burial customs. Additionally, comparative studies with other tomb types help shed light on the social structure and power dynamics of the Kofun period. == History == In the latter half to the end of the sixth century, as the keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] that had previously served as chieftain tombs [首長墓] went into decline and disappeared, a new type of final-stage square tumulus [方墳] emerged. Unlike earlier square tumuli [方墳], these final-stage square tumuli [方墳] appeared as a new burial form for sovereigns [大王墓] or chieftains [首長墓].https://adeac.jp/yukuhashi-city/text-list/d100010/ht1024406020 The Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Yōmei [伝用明天皇陵]), dated to the end of the sixth century through the early seventh century, measures 65 meters east-to-west and 60 meters north-to-south. Similarly, the Akasaka Tennozan Kofun in Nara Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Sushun [伝崇峻天皇陵]) measures 45.5 meters east-to-west and 42.2 meters north-to-south. The Yamada Takatsuka Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Empress Suiko [伝推古天皇陵]), from around the first half of the seventh century, measures 59 meters east-to-west and 55 meters north-to-south. All of these are rectangular tumuli [長方形墳]. The Ishibutai Kofun in Nara Prefecture, said to be the tomb of Soga no Umako from around the first half of the seventh century, is a square tumulus [方墳] measuring 51 meters on each side. Likewise, the Iwayayama Kofun from the middle of the seventh century is said to be a round-top, square-bottom tumulus [上円下方墳] with each side measuring 45 meters. From the end of the sixth century through the first half of the seventh century, it appears that slightly elongated rectangular tumuli [長方形墳] were standardized as replacements for keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] for use as sovereigns’ tombs [大王墓] or chieftains’ tombs [首長墓]. == See Also == * Kofun * Keyhole-shaped tomb (''zenpō-kōenfun'', 前方後円墳) * Circular tomb (''empun'', 円墳) * Square tomb (''hōfun'', 方墳) * Kofun period === References === * Japanese Historical Society, ''Archaeology of the Kofun Period'', University of Tokyo Press, 1995. * Sahara Makoto, ''Kofun and the Ancient State'', Iwanami Shoten, 2000. == List == * {{ill|Amamiyama Kofun|ja|安満宮山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Anman Miyayama Kofun|qq=}}

But I think this might be a mistranslation[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:29, 1 December 2023 (UTC)}} {{Afc comment|1=This is the one Kofun type that is not covered by Japanese wikipedia. It is unclear how notable it is but there is a Category[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 20:41, 23 October 2023 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=If this times out then delete the Category since the only mainspace member of the Category [[:en:Umamukaiyama Kofun|Umamukaiyama Kofun]] is also in the {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} Category[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:38, 23 October 2023 (UTC) – draft}} {{nihongo|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|長方形墳}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] They often have multiple rooms for burials.https://kofun.info/tag/14 File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun,_funkyu.jpg|Umamukaiyama Kofun File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_genshitsu-1.jpg|No.1 Burial Chamber, far end File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_sendou-2.jpg|No1 Burial Chamber, entry [[File:Uma Mukaiyama Kofun-1, entrance.jpg|thumb|[[:en:Umamukaiyama Kofun|Umamukaiyama Kofun]]]] '''Rectangular Tombs (長方形墳, Chōhōkeifun)''' A ''rectangular tomb'' (''chōhōkeifun'') is a type of Kofun (kofun) constructed during the Kofun period, characterized by a rectangular-shaped Kofun. These tombs are found across Japan and exhibit a variety of sizes and structures depending on the region and time period. === Characteristics === As the name suggests, rectangular tombs have a rectangular-shaped mound when viewed from above. The size of these mounds varies, ranging from small-scale to large-scale constructions. Some tombs feature surrounding moats (''shūgō'', 周濠) or embankments (''shūtei'', 周堤), and burial facilities within them may include ''tateana-shiki sekishitsu'' (pit-style stone chambers) or ''yokoana-shiki sekishitsu'' (horizontal stone chambers). === Distribution and Period === Rectangular tombs were primarily built from the mid to late Kofun period. They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. === Significance === The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. These tombs serve as important archaeological resources for understanding regional cultural characteristics and burial customs. Additionally, comparative studies with other tomb types help shed light on the social structure and power dynamics of the Kofun period. == History == In the latter half to the end of the sixth century, as the keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] that had previously served as chieftain tombs [首長墓] went into decline and disappeared, a new type of final-stage square tumulus [方墳] emerged. Unlike earlier square tumuli [方墳], these final-stage square tumuli [方墳] appeared as a new burial form for sovereigns [大王墓] or chieftains [首長墓].https://adeac.jp/yukuhashi-city/text-list/d100010/ht1024406020 The Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Yōmei [伝用明天皇陵]), dated to the end of the sixth century through the early seventh century, measures 65 meters east-to-west and 60 meters north-to-south. Similarly, the Akasaka Tennozan Kofun in Nara Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Sushun [伝崇峻天皇陵]) measures 45.5 meters east-to-west and 42.2 meters north-to-south. The Yamada Takatsuka Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Empress Suiko [伝推古天皇陵]), from around the first half of the seventh century, measures 59 meters east-to-west and 55 meters north-to-south. All of these are rectangular tumuli [長方形墳]. The Ishibutai Kofun in Nara Prefecture, said to be the tomb of Soga no Umako from around the first half of the seventh century, is a square tumulus [方墳] measuring 51 meters on each side. Likewise, the Iwayayama Kofun from the middle of the seventh century is said to be a round-top, square-bottom tumulus [上円下方墳] with each side measuring 45 meters. From the end of the sixth century through the first half of the seventh century, it appears that slightly elongated rectangular tumuli [長方形墳] were standardized as replacements for keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] for use as sovereigns’ tombs [大王墓] or chieftains’ tombs [首長墓]. == See Also == * Kofun * Keyhole-shaped tomb (''zenpō-kōenfun'', 前方後円墳) * Circular tomb (''empun'', 円墳) * Square tomb (''hōfun'', 方墳) * Kofun period === References === * Japanese Historical Society, ''Archaeology of the Kofun Period'', University of Tokyo Press, 1995. * Sahara Makoto, ''Kofun and the Ancient State'', Iwanami Shoten, 2000. == List == * {{ill|Amamiyama Kofun|ja|安満宮山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Anman Miyayama Kofun|qq=}}

But I think this might be a mistranslation[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:29, 1 December 2023 (UTC)}} {{Afc comment|1=This is the one Kofun type that is not covered by Japanese wikipedia. It is unclear how notable it is but there is a Category[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 20:41, 23 October 2023 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=If this times out then delete the Category since the only mainspace member of the Category [[:en:Umamukaiyama Kofun|Umamukaiyama Kofun]] is also in the {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} Category[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:38, 23 October 2023 (UTC) – draft}} {{nihongo|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|長方形墳}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] They often have multiple rooms for burials.https://kofun.info/tag/14 File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun,_funkyu.jpg|Umamukaiyama Kofun File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_genshitsu-1.jpg|No.1 Burial Chamber, far end File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_sendou-2.jpg|No1 Burial Chamber, entry [[File:Uma Mukaiyama Kofun-1, entrance.jpg|thumb|[[:en:Umamukaiyama Kofun|Umamukaiyama Kofun]]]] '''Rectangular Tombs (長方形墳, Chōhōkeifun)''' A ''rectangular tomb'' (''chōhōkeifun'') is a type of Kofun (kofun) constructed during the Kofun period, characterized by a rectangular-shaped Kofun. These tombs are found across Japan and exhibit a variety of sizes and structures depending on the region and time period. === Characteristics === As the name suggests, rectangular tombs have a rectangular-shaped mound when viewed from above. The size of these mounds varies, ranging from small-scale to large-scale constructions. Some tombs feature surrounding moats (''shūgō'', 周濠) or embankments (''shūtei'', 周堤), and burial facilities within them may include ''tateana-shiki sekishitsu'' (pit-style stone chambers) or ''yokoana-shiki sekishitsu'' (horizontal stone chambers). === Distribution and Period === Rectangular tombs were primarily built from the mid to late Kofun period. They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. === Significance === The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. These tombs serve as important archaeological resources for understanding regional cultural characteristics and burial customs. Additionally, comparative studies with other tomb types help shed light on the social structure and power dynamics of the Kofun period. == History == In the latter half to the end of the sixth century, as the keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] that had previously served as chieftain tombs [首長墓] went into decline and disappeared, a new type of final-stage square tumulus [方墳] emerged. Unlike earlier square tumuli [方墳], these final-stage square tumuli [方墳] appeared as a new burial form for sovereigns [大王墓] or chieftains [首長墓].https://adeac.jp/yukuhashi-city/text-list/d100010/ht1024406020 The Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Yōmei [伝用明天皇陵]), dated to the end of the sixth century through the early seventh century, measures 65 meters east-to-west and 60 meters north-to-south. Similarly, the Akasaka Tennozan Kofun in Nara Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Sushun [伝崇峻天皇陵]) measures 45.5 meters east-to-west and 42.2 meters north-to-south. The Yamada Takatsuka Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Empress Suiko [伝推古天皇陵]), from around the first half of the seventh century, measures 59 meters east-to-west and 55 meters north-to-south. All of these are rectangular tumuli [長方形墳]. The Ishibutai Kofun in Nara Prefecture, said to be the tomb of Soga no Umako from around the first half of the seventh century, is a square tumulus [方墳] measuring 51 meters on each side. Likewise, the Iwayayama Kofun from the middle of the seventh century is said to be a round-top, square-bottom tumulus [上円下方墳] with each side measuring 45 meters. From the end of the sixth century through the first half of the seventh century, it appears that slightly elongated rectangular tumuli [長方形墳] were standardized as replacements for keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] for use as sovereigns’ tombs [大王墓] or chieftains’ tombs [首長墓]. == See Also == * Kofun * Keyhole-shaped tomb (''zenpō-kōenfun'', 前方後円墳) * Circular tomb (''empun'', 円墳) * Square tomb (''hōfun'', 方墳) * Kofun period === References === * Japanese Historical Society, ''Archaeology of the Kofun Period'', University of Tokyo Press, 1995. * Sahara Makoto, ''Kofun and the Ancient State'', Iwanami Shoten, 2000. == List == * {{ill|Amamiyama Kofun|ja|安満宮山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Anman Miyayama Kofun|qq=}}

It is unclear how notable it is but there is a Category[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 20:41, 23 October 2023 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=If this times out then delete the Category since the only mainspace member of the Category [[:en:Umamukaiyama Kofun|Umamukaiyama Kofun]] is also in the {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} Category[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:38, 23 October 2023 (UTC) – draft}} {{nihongo|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|長方形墳}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] They often have multiple rooms for burials.https://kofun.info/tag/14 File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun,_funkyu.jpg|Umamukaiyama Kofun File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_genshitsu-1.jpg|No.1 Burial Chamber, far end File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_sendou-2.jpg|No1 Burial Chamber, entry [[File:Uma Mukaiyama Kofun-1, entrance.jpg|thumb|[[:en:Umamukaiyama Kofun|Umamukaiyama Kofun]]]] == '''Rectangular Tombs (長方形墳, Chōhōkeifun)''' == A ''rectangular tomb'' (''chōhōkeifun'') is a type of Kofun (kofun) constructed during the Kofun period, characterized by a rectangular-shaped Kofun. These tombs are found across Japan and exhibit a variety of sizes and structures depending on the region and time period. == Characteristics == As the name suggests, rectangular tombs have a rectangular-shaped mound when viewed from above. The size of these mounds varies, ranging from small-scale to large-scale constructions. Some tombs feature surrounding moats (''shūgō'', 周濠) or embankments (''shūtei'', 周堤), and burial facilities within them may include ''tateana-shiki sekishitsu'' (pit-style stone chambers) or ''yokoana-shiki sekishitsu'' (horizontal stone chambers). == Distribution and Period == Rectangular tombs were primarily built from the mid to late Kofun period. They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. == Significance == The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. These tombs serve as important archaeological resources for understanding regional cultural characteristics and burial customs. Additionally, comparative studies with other tomb types help shed light on the social structure and power dynamics of the Kofun period. == History == In the latter half to the end of the sixth century, as the keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] that had previously served as chieftain tombs [首長墓] went into decline and disappeared, a new type of final-stage square tumulus [方墳] emerged. Unlike earlier square tumuli [方墳], these final-stage square tumuli [方墳] appeared as a new burial form for sovereigns [大王墓] or chieftains [首長墓].https://adeac.jp/yukuhashi-city/text-list/d100010/ht1024406020 The Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Yōmei [伝用明天皇陵]), dated to the end of the sixth century through the early seventh century, measures 65 meters east-to-west and 60 meters north-to-south. Similarly, the Akasaka Tennozan Kofun in Nara Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Sushun [伝崇峻天皇陵]) measures 45.5 meters east-to-west and 42.2 meters north-to-south. The Yamada Takatsuka Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Empress Suiko [伝推古天皇陵]), from around the first half of the seventh century, measures 59 meters east-to-west and 55 meters north-to-south. All of these are rectangular tumuli [長方形墳]. The Ishibutai Kofun in Nara Prefecture, said to be the tomb of Soga no Umako from around the first half of the seventh century, is a square tumulus [方墳] measuring 51 meters on each side. Likewise, the Iwayayama Kofun from the middle of the seventh century is said to be a round-top, square-bottom tumulus [上円下方墳] with each side measuring 45 meters. From the end of the sixth century through the first half of the seventh century, it appears that slightly elongated rectangular tumuli [長方形墳] were standardized as replacements for keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] for use as sovereigns’ tombs [大王墓] or chieftains’ tombs [首長墓]. * == List == * {{ill|Amamiyama Kofun|ja|安満宮山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Anman Miyayama Kofun|qq=}}

It is unclear how notable it is but there is a Category[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 20:41, 23 October 2023 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=If this times out then delete the Category since the only mainspace member of the Category [[:en:Umamukaiyama Kofun|Umamukaiyama Kofun]] is also in the {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} Category[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:38, 23 October 2023 (UTC) – draft}} {{nihongo|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|長方形墳}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] They often have multiple rooms for burials.https://kofun.info/tag/14 File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun,_funkyu.jpg|Umamukaiyama Kofun File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_genshitsu-1.jpg|No.1 Burial Chamber, far end File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_sendou-2.jpg|No1 Burial Chamber, entry [[File:Uma Mukaiyama Kofun-1, entrance.jpg|thumb|[[:en:Umamukaiyama Kofun|Umamukaiyama Kofun]]]] == '''Rectangular Tombs (長方形墳, Chōhōkeifun)''' == A ''rectangular tomb'' (''chōhōkeifun'') is a type of Kofun (kofun) constructed during the Kofun period, characterized by a rectangular-shaped Kofun. These tombs are found across Japan and exhibit a variety of sizes and structures depending on the region and time period. == Characteristics == As the name suggests, rectangular tombs have a rectangular-shaped mound when viewed from above. The size of these mounds varies, ranging from small-scale to large-scale constructions. Some tombs feature surrounding moats (''shūgō'', 周濠) or embankments (''shūtei'', 周堤), and burial facilities within them may include ''tateana-shiki sekishitsu'' (pit-style stone chambers) or ''yokoana-shiki sekishitsu'' (horizontal stone chambers). == Distribution and Period == Rectangular tombs were primarily built from the mid to late Kofun period. They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. == Significance == The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. These tombs serve as important archaeological resources for understanding regional cultural characteristics and burial customs. Additionally, comparative studies with other tomb types help shed light on the social structure and power dynamics of the Kofun period. == History == In the latter half to the end of the sixth century, as the keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] that had previously served as chieftain tombs [首長墓] went into decline and disappeared, a new type of final-stage square tumulus [方墳] emerged. Unlike earlier square tumuli [方墳], these final-stage square tumuli [方墳] appeared as a new burial form for sovereigns [大王墓] or chieftains [首長墓].https://adeac.jp/yukuhashi-city/text-list/d100010/ht1024406020 The Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Yōmei [伝用明天皇陵]), dated to the end of the sixth century through the early seventh century, measures 65 meters east-to-west and 60 meters north-to-south. Similarly, the Akasaka Tennozan Kofun in Nara Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Sushun [伝崇峻天皇陵]) measures 45.5 meters east-to-west and 42.2 meters north-to-south. The Yamada Takatsuka Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Empress Suiko [伝推古天皇陵]), from around the first half of the seventh century, measures 59 meters east-to-west and 55 meters north-to-south. All of these are rectangular tumuli [長方形墳]. The Ishibutai Kofun in Nara Prefecture, said to be the tomb of Soga no Umako from around the first half of the seventh century, is a square tumulus [方墳] measuring 51 meters on each side. Likewise, the Iwayayama Kofun from the middle of the seventh century is said to be a round-top, square-bottom tumulus [上円下方墳] with each side measuring 45 meters. From the end of the sixth century through the first half of the seventh century, it appears that slightly elongated rectangular tumuli [長方形墳] were standardized as replacements for keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] for use as sovereigns’ tombs [大王墓] or chieftains’ tombs [首長墓]. * == List == * {{ill|Amamiyama Kofun|ja|安満宮山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Anman Miyayama Kofun|qq=}}

is also in the {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square-type|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} Category[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 22:38, 23 October 2023 (UTC) – draft}} {{nihongo|Rectangular Kofun|lt=Rectangular Kofun|長方形墳}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] They often have multiple rooms for burials.https://kofun.info/tag/14 File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun,_funkyu.jpg|Umamukaiyama Kofun File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_genshitsu-1.jpg|No.1 Burial Chamber, far end File:Uma_Mukaiyama_Kofun-1,_sendou-2.jpg|No1 Burial Chamber, entry [[File:Uma Mukaiyama Kofun-1, entrance.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Umamukaiyama Kofun|en|Umamukaiyama Kofun|WD=Q11449416|lt=Umamukaiyama Kofun}}]] == '''Rectangular Tombs (長方形墳, Chōhōkeifun)''' == A ''rectangular tomb'' (''chōhōkeifun'') is a type of Kofun (kofun) constructed during the Kofun period, characterized by a rectangular-shaped Kofun. These tombs are found across Japan and exhibit a variety of sizes and structures depending on the region and time period. == Characteristics == As the name suggests, rectangular tombs have a rectangular-shaped mound when viewed from above. The size of these mounds varies, ranging from small-scale to large-scale constructions. Some tombs feature surrounding moats (''shūgō'', 周濠) or embankments (''shūtei'', 周堤), and burial facilities within them may include ''tateana-shiki sekishitsu'' (pit-style stone chambers) or ''yokoana-shiki sekishitsu'' (horizontal stone chambers). == Distribution and Period == Rectangular tombs were primarily built from the mid to late Kofun period. They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. == Significance == The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. These tombs serve as important archaeological resources for understanding regional cultural characteristics and burial customs. Additionally, comparative studies with other tomb types help shed light on the social structure and power dynamics of the Kofun period. == History == In the latter half to the end of the sixth century, as the keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] that had previously served as chieftain tombs [首長墓] went into decline and disappeared, a new type of final-stage square tumulus [方墳] emerged. Unlike earlier square tumuli [方墳], these final-stage square tumuli [方墳] appeared as a new burial form for sovereigns [大王墓] or chieftains [首長墓].https://adeac.jp/yukuhashi-city/text-list/d100010/ht1024406020 The Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Yōmei [伝用明天皇陵]), dated to the end of the sixth century through the early seventh century, measures 65 meters east-to-west and 60 meters north-to-south. Similarly, the Akasaka Tennōzan Kofun in Nara Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Sushun [伝崇峻天皇陵]) measures 45.5 meters east-to-west and 42.2 meters north-to-south. The Yamada Takatsuka Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Empress Suiko [伝推古天皇陵]), from around the first half of the seventh century, measures 59 meters east-to-west and 55 meters north-to-south. All of these are rectangular tumuli [長方形墳]. The Ishibutai Kofun in Nara Prefecture, said to be the tomb of Soga no Umako from around the first half of the seventh century, is a square tumulus [方墳] measuring 51 meters on each side. Likewise, the Iwayayama Kofun from the middle of the seventh century is said to be a round-top, square-bottom tumulus [上円下方墳] with each side measuring 45 meters. From the end of the sixth century through the first half of the seventh century, it appears that slightly elongated rectangular tumuli [長方形墳] were standardized as replacements for keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] for use as sovereigns’ tombs [大王墓] or chieftains’ tombs [首長墓]. * == List == * {{ill|Amamiyama Kofun|ja|安満宮山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Anman Miyayama Kofun|qq=}}

These tombs are found across Japan and exhibit a variety of sizes and structures depending on the region and time period. == Characteristics == As the name suggests, rectangular tombs have a rectangular-shaped mound when viewed from above. The size of these mounds varies, ranging from small-scale to large-scale constructions. Some tombs feature surrounding moats (''shūgō'', 周濠) or embankments (''shūtei'', 周堤), and burial facilities within them may include ''tateana-shiki sekishitsu'' (pit-style stone chambers) or ''yokoana-shiki sekishitsu'' (horizontal stone chambers). == Distribution and Period == Rectangular tombs were primarily built from the mid to late Kofun period. They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. == Significance == The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. These tombs serve as important archaeological resources for understanding regional cultural characteristics and burial customs. Additionally, comparative studies with other tomb types help shed light on the social structure and power dynamics of the Kofun period. == History == In the latter half to the end of the sixth century, as the keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] that had previously served as chieftain tombs [首長墓] went into decline and disappeared, a new type of final-stage square tumulus [方墳] emerged. Unlike earlier square tumuli [方墳], these final-stage square tumuli [方墳] appeared as a new burial form for sovereigns [大王墓] or chieftains [首長墓].https://adeac.jp/yukuhashi-city/text-list/d100010/ht1024406020 The Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Yōmei [伝用明天皇陵]), dated to the end of the sixth century through the early seventh century, measures 65 meters east-to-west and 60 meters north-to-south. Similarly, the Akasaka Tennōzan Kofun in Nara Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Sushun [伝崇峻天皇陵]) measures 45.5 meters east-to-west and 42.2 meters north-to-south. The Yamada Takatsuka Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Empress Suiko [伝推古天皇陵]), from around the first half of the seventh century, measures 59 meters east-to-west and 55 meters north-to-south. All of these are rectangular tumuli [長方形墳]. The Ishibutai Kofun in Nara Prefecture, said to be the tomb of Soga no Umako from around the first half of the seventh century, is a square tumulus [方墳] measuring 51 meters on each side. Likewise, the Iwayayama Kofun from the middle of the seventh century is said to be a round-top, square-bottom tumulus [上円下方墳] with each side measuring 45 meters. From the end of the sixth century through the first half of the seventh century, it appears that slightly elongated rectangular tumuli [長方形墳] were standardized as replacements for keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] for use as sovereigns’ tombs [大王墓] or chieftains’ tombs [首長墓]. * == List == * {{ill|Amamiyama Kofun|ja|安満宮山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Anman Miyayama Kofun|qq=}}

They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. == Significance == The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. They are most commonly found in regions such as the Kinki (Kansai) and Chūgoku areas but have also been identified in other parts of Japan. The distribution and construction periods of these tombs are thought to reflect the political and social structures of the time, as well as interregional interactions. == Significance == The construction of rectangular tombs highlights the diversity of burial practices among rulers and influential figures of the time. These tombs serve as important archaeological resources for understanding regional cultural characteristics and burial customs. Additionally, comparative studies with other tomb types help shed light on the social structure and power dynamics of the Kofun period. == History == In the latter half to the end of the sixth century, as the keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] that had previously served as chieftain tombs [首長墓] went into decline and disappeared, a new type of final-stage square tumulus [方墳] emerged. Unlike earlier square tumuli [方墳], these final-stage square tumuli [方墳] appeared as a new burial form for sovereigns [大王墓] or chieftains [首長墓].https://adeac.jp/yukuhashi-city/text-list/d100010/ht1024406020 The Kasuga Mukoyama Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Yōmei [伝用明天皇陵]), dated to the end of the sixth century through the early seventh century, measures 65 meters east-to-west and 60 meters north-to-south. Similarly, the Akasaka Tennōzan Kofun in Nara Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Emperor Sushun [伝崇峻天皇陵]) measures 45.5 meters east-to-west and 42.2 meters north-to-south. The Yamada Takatsuka Kofun in Osaka Prefecture (traditionally attributed to Empress Suiko [伝推古天皇陵]), from around the first half of the seventh century, measures 59 meters east-to-west and 55 meters north-to-south. All of these are rectangular tumuli [長方形墳]. The Ishibutai Kofun in Nara Prefecture, said to be the tomb of Soga no Umako from around the first half of the seventh century, is a square tumulus [方墳] measuring 51 meters on each side. Likewise, the Iwayayama Kofun from the middle of the seventh century is said to be a round-top, square-bottom tumulus [上円下方墳] with each side measuring 45 meters. From the end of the sixth century through the first half of the seventh century, it appears that slightly elongated rectangular tumuli [長方形墳] were standardized as replacements for keyhole-shaped tumuli [前方後円墳] for use as sovereigns’ tombs [大王墓] or chieftains’ tombs [首長墓]. * == List == * {{ill|Amamiyama Kofun|ja|安満宮山古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Anman Miyayama Kofun|qq=}}
